cards.name: Frontal lobe
cards.function: Largest lobe of the cerebral hemisphere, in front of the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus; contains the primary motor cortex, premotor areas, frontal eye field, motor speech area and prefrontal cortex.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior cranial fossa, on the orbital plate of the frontal bone; from the frontal pole back to the central sulcus (of Rolando), bounded below by the lateral sulcus (of Sylvius)

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Precentral gyrus; superior, middle and inferior frontal gyri (separated by the superior and inferior frontal sulci); medial frontal gyrus and paracentral lobule on the medial surface; straight gyrus and orbital gyri on the inferior surface

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (medial and superior surface) and middle cerebral artery (lateral surface)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Central sulcus separates it from the parietal lobe; lateral sulcus from the temporal lobe; frontal operculum covers the insula

cards.pearl: Frontal lobe lesions cause contralateral weakness, personality change and disinhibition, and return of primitive reflexes; a frontal eye field lesion deviates the eyes toward the side of the lesion.

cards.name: Frontal pole
cards.function: Most anterior point of the cerebral hemisphere; its cortex is prefrontal association cortex concerned with planning and judgement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior end of the frontal lobe, behind the squamous part of the frontal bone in the anterior cranial fossa

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior, middle and inferior frontal gyri converge on it; orbital gyri lie below it; the two poles are separated by the longitudinal cerebral fissure and falx cerebri

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (medial frontobasal and polar branches)

cards.pearl: The frontal and temporal poles are the classic sites of contrecoup contusion after an occipital blow.

cards.name: Precentral gyrus
cards.function: Primary motor cortex: origin of much of the corticospinal and corticonuclear tracts controlling voluntary movement of the contralateral body, arranged as a motor homunculus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Frontal lobe, between the precentral sulcus in front and the central sulcus (of Rolando) behind; continues onto the medial surface as the anterior part of the paracentral lobule

details.label: Function
details.value: Face and hand are represented on the lateral surface, the leg and foot on the medial surface in the paracentral lobule

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (arteries of the precentral and central sulci) for face and arm; anterior cerebral artery for the leg area

details.label: Relations
details.value: Postcentral gyrus behind; opercular part of the inferior frontal gyrus below and in front

cards.pearl: Middle cerebral artery stroke gives contralateral face and arm weakness greater than leg; anterior cerebral artery stroke gives contralateral leg weakness.

cards.name: Precentral sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that forms the anterior boundary of the precentral gyrus, separating primary motor cortex from the premotor cortex of the frontal gyri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the frontal lobe, parallel to and in front of the central sulcus

details.label: Parts
details.value: Often interrupted into a superior and an inferior part; the superior frontal sulcus joins the superior part and the inferior frontal sulcus joins the inferior part

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precentral gyrus behind; superior, middle and inferior frontal gyri in front; artery of the precentral sulcus runs in it

cards.name: Central sulcus (of Rolando)
cards.function: Boundary between the frontal and parietal lobes, separating the primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus) from the primary somatosensory cortex (postcentral gyrus).

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs from the superior margin of the hemisphere downward and forward toward, but usually not into, the lateral sulcus; notches the medial surface within the paracentral lobule

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precentral gyrus in front, postcentral gyrus behind; a separate central sulcus of the insula lies deep to it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Artery of the central sulcus (middle cerebral artery) runs in it

cards.pearl: On axial imaging the central sulcus is found by the inverted-omega "hand knob" of the precentral gyrus; it is the key landmark when planning surgery near motor cortex.

cards.name: Superior frontal gyrus
cards.function: Uppermost frontal gyrus; its posterior part contains premotor and supplementary motor cortex concerned with planning and initiating movement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Along the superior margin of the frontal lobe, above the superior frontal sulcus; continuous over the margin with the medial frontal gyrus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Middle frontal gyrus below; precentral sulcus and gyrus behind; falx cerebri and superior sagittal sinus medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (callosomarginal branches) with middle cerebral artery laterally

cards.pearl: A lesion of the supplementary motor area causes transient contralateral akinesia and mutism that typically recovers.

cards.name: Superior frontal sulcus
cards.function: Sagittally running sulcus that separates the superior from the middle frontal gyrus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the frontal lobe, running forward from the precentral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior frontal gyrus above, middle frontal gyrus below; its junction with the precentral sulcus marks the level of the hand area of the precentral gyrus

cards.name: Middle frontal gyrus
cards.function: Middle of the three frontal gyri; contains the frontal eye field posteriorly and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex anteriorly (executive function, working memory).

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the frontal lobe between the superior and inferior frontal sulci

details.label: Function
details.value: Frontal eye field drives conjugate gaze to the opposite side; dorsolateral prefrontal cortex supports planning and attention

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (prefrontal artery and artery of the precentral sulcus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior frontal gyrus above, inferior frontal gyrus below, precentral gyrus behind

cards.pearl: A destructive frontal eye field lesion makes the eyes look toward the lesion (away from the hemiparesis); a seizure focus there drives them away.

cards.name: Inferior frontal sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that separates the middle frontal gyrus from the inferior frontal gyrus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the frontal lobe, running forward from the inferior part of the precentral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Middle frontal gyrus above; opercular, triangular and orbital parts of the inferior frontal gyrus below

cards.name: Inferior frontal gyrus
cards.function: Lowest frontal gyrus, forming the frontal operculum over the insula; in the dominant hemisphere its opercular and triangular parts form the motor speech area (of Broca).

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the frontal lobe below the inferior frontal sulcus and above the lateral sulcus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Opercular part, triangular part and orbital part, separated by the ascending ramus and anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery, superior division (prefrontal and lateral frontobasal arteries)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precentral gyrus behind; insula deep to it; orbital gyri below and in front

cards.pearl: Broca (nonfluent, expressive) aphasia: effortful telegraphic speech with preserved comprehension and impaired repetition, from a dominant superior-division middle cerebral artery stroke.

cards.name: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus
cards.function: Posterior part of the inferior frontal gyrus; with the triangular part forms the motor speech area in the dominant hemisphere.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the precentral sulcus behind and the ascending ramus of the lateral sulcus in front

details.label: Relations
details.value: Face area of the precentral gyrus behind; triangular part in front; forms part of the frontal operculum covering the insula

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (artery of the precentral sulcus, prefrontal artery)

cards.pearl: Because it adjoins the face area of the motor cortex, Broca aphasia is usually accompanied by contralateral lower facial and arm weakness.

cards.name: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus
cards.function: Wedge-shaped middle part of the inferior frontal gyrus; with the opercular part forms the motor speech area in the dominant hemisphere.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the ascending ramus and the anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Opercular part behind, orbital part below and in front; overlies the anterior insula

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (prefrontal artery)

cards.name: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus
cards.function: Anteroinferior part of the inferior frontal gyrus, continuous with the orbital gyri; prefrontal association cortex.

details.label: Location
details.value: Below the anterior ramus of the lateral sulcus, curving onto the orbital surface of the frontal lobe

details.label: Relations
details.value: Triangular part above and behind; orbital gyri medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (lateral frontobasal artery)

cards.name: Medial frontal gyrus
cards.function: Medial surface of the superior frontal gyrus; contains the supplementary motor area posteriorly and medial prefrontal cortex anteriorly (motivation, initiation of behavior).

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the frontal lobe above the cingulate sulcus, in front of the paracentral sulcus and paracentral lobule

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cingulate gyrus below; falx cerebri medially; continuous over the superior margin with the superior frontal gyrus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (callosomarginal artery)

cards.pearl: Bilateral medial frontal damage (anterior cerebral artery infarcts) causes abulia or akinetic mutism.

cards.name: Paracentral lobule
cards.function: Medial continuation of the precentral and postcentral gyri around the end of the central sulcus; motor and sensory cortex for the contralateral leg, foot and perineum, with cortical control of micturition.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the hemisphere between the paracentral sulcus in front and the marginal sulcus behind, above the cingulate sulcus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (callosomarginal and pericallosal arteries)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medial frontal gyrus in front, precuneus behind, cingulate gyrus below; the central sulcus notches its upper border

cards.pearl: Anterior cerebral artery occlusion: contralateral leg weakness and sensory loss with urinary incontinence; a parasagittal meningioma can cause bilateral leg weakness that mimics cord disease.

cards.name: Straight gyrus
cards.function: Narrow gyrus on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe medial to the olfactory sulcus; orbitofrontal association cortex.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the frontal lobe, between the longitudinal cerebral fissure medially and the olfactory sulcus laterally

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory bulb and tract lie lateral to it in the olfactory sulcus; rests on the cribriform plate and orbital plate; orbital gyri lateral

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (medial frontobasal artery)

cards.pearl: An olfactory groove meningioma compresses the straight gyri and olfactory tracts: anosmia with frontal lobe personality change.

cards.name: Olfactory sulcus
cards.function: Sagittal sulcus on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe that lodges the olfactory bulb and olfactory tract.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the frontal lobe, parallel to the longitudinal cerebral fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Straight gyrus medially, orbital gyri laterally; the olfactory tract runs back in it to the anterior perforated substance

cards.name: Orbital gyri and orbital sulci
cards.function: Gyri on the orbital surface of the frontal lobe, divided by the H-shaped orbital sulci; orbitofrontal cortex concerned with social behavior, impulse control and reward.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the frontal lobe, lateral to the olfactory sulcus, resting on the orbital plate of the frontal bone

details.label: Parts
details.value: The orbital sulci form an H that separates anterior, posterior, medial and lateral orbital gyri

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Medial frontobasal artery (anterior cerebral) and lateral frontobasal artery (middle cerebral)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Straight gyrus and olfactory tract medially; orbital part of the inferior frontal gyrus laterally; frontal pole in front

cards.pearl: Orbitofrontal injury (trauma, frontotemporal dementia) produces disinhibition, poor judgement and socially inappropriate behavior.

cards.name: Lateral sulcus (of Sylvius)
cards.function: Deep fissure separating the frontal and parietal lobes above from the temporal lobe below; the insula lies in its floor and the middle cerebral artery branches run within it.

details.label: Location
details.value: Begins on the inferior surface at the anterior perforated substance, passes laterally between the frontal lobe and temporal pole, then runs back on the lateral surface

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior ramus, ascending ramus and posterior ramus; the anterior and ascending rami cut into the inferior frontal gyrus and the posterior ramus ends in the supramarginal gyrus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Frontal, parietal and temporal opercula form its lips and cover the insula; superficial middle cerebral vein runs along it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery and its branches lie in the sulcus

cards.pearl: A middle cerebral artery (berry) aneurysm at its bifurcation ruptures into the lateral sulcus; blood in the Sylvian fissure on CT suggests this source.

cards.name: Insula (island of Reil)
cards.function: Buried lobe of cortex in the floor of the lateral sulcus; involved in taste, visceral sensation, pain and autonomic control.

details.label: Location
details.value: Deep to the frontal, parietal and temporal opercula; lateral to the extreme capsule, claustrum and lentiform nucleus

details.label: Parts
details.value: Short gyri anteriorly and long gyrus posteriorly, separated by the central sulcus of the insula; limen at its anteroinferior apex; bounded by the circular sulcus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Insular branches of the middle cerebral artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Middle cerebral artery branches lie on its surface; extreme capsule, claustrum, external capsule and putamen lie deep to it

cards.pearl: Loss of the "insular ribbon" (gray-white differentiation of the insula) is an early CT sign of middle cerebral artery infarction.

cards.name: Parietal lobe
cards.function: Lobe behind the central sulcus containing primary somatosensory cortex and association cortex for spatial awareness, attention and (dominant side) language and calculation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the central sulcus in front and the parieto-occipital sulcus behind, above the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Postcentral gyrus; superior parietal lobule; inferior parietal lobule (supramarginal gyrus and angular gyrus); precuneus on the medial surface

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (lateral surface), anterior cerebral artery (medial surface), posterior cerebral artery (posterior precuneus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parietal operculum covers the insula; optic radiation passes through its deep white matter

cards.pearl: Nondominant parietal lesion: contralateral hemispatial neglect. Dominant inferior parietal lesion: Gerstmann syndrome. Either side: contralateral inferior quadrantanopia.

cards.name: Postcentral gyrus
cards.function: Primary somatosensory cortex receiving touch, proprioception, pain and temperature from the contralateral body through the ventral posterolateral and ventral posteromedial thalamic nuclei.

details.label: Location
details.value: Parietal lobe between the central sulcus in front and the postcentral sulcus behind; continues medially as the posterior part of the paracentral lobule

details.label: Function
details.value: Sensory homunculus: face and hand laterally, leg and foot medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (arteries of the central and postcentral sulci); anterior cerebral artery for the leg area

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precentral gyrus in front; superior and inferior parietal lobules behind

cards.pearl: Cortical sensory loss: impaired two-point discrimination, astereognosis and agraphesthesia of the contralateral side with relatively preserved crude touch.

cards.name: Postcentral sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that forms the posterior boundary of the postcentral gyrus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the parietal lobe, parallel to and behind the central sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Postcentral gyrus in front; superior and inferior parietal lobules behind; the intraparietal sulcus runs back from it; artery of the postcentral sulcus runs in it

cards.name: Superior parietal lobule
cards.function: Somatosensory and visuospatial association cortex that integrates touch, proprioception and vision to guide reaching.

details.label: Location
details.value: Parietal lobe above the intraparietal sulcus, behind the postcentral sulcus; continuous medially with the precuneus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior parietal lobule below; parieto-occipital sulcus behind

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (posterior parietal artery) and anterior cerebral artery near the superior margin

cards.pearl: Lesions cause contralateral astereognosis and optic ataxia (misreaching under visual guidance).

cards.name: Intraparietal sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that divides the parietal lobe behind the postcentral gyrus into superior and inferior parietal lobules.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the parietal lobe, running back from the postcentral sulcus toward the occipital lobe

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior parietal lobule above; supramarginal and angular gyri below

cards.name: Inferior parietal lobule
cards.function: Multimodal association cortex below the intraparietal sulcus; in the dominant hemisphere it supports reading, writing and calculation, in the nondominant hemisphere spatial attention.

details.label: Location
details.value: Parietal lobe below the intraparietal sulcus, around the upturned ends of the lateral sulcus and superior temporal sulcus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Supramarginal gyrus (anterior) and angular gyrus (posterior), separated by a small inconstant intermediate sulcus (of Jensen)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (posterior parietal artery and artery to the angular gyrus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior parietal lobule above; superior temporal gyrus below; parietal operculum covers the insula

cards.pearl: Nondominant lesion: contralateral neglect, anosognosia and constructional apraxia.

cards.name: Supramarginal gyrus
cards.function: Anterior part of the inferior parietal lobule; phonological processing and language repetition in the dominant hemisphere.

details.label: Location
details.value: Arches over the upturned end of the posterior ramus of the lateral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Postcentral gyrus in front, angular gyrus behind, superior temporal gyrus below; the arcuate fasciculus runs deep to it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (posterior parietal artery)

cards.pearl: Conduction aphasia (fluent speech, good comprehension, poor repetition) follows damage to the supramarginal gyrus and underlying arcuate fasciculus.

cards.name: Angular gyrus
cards.function: Posterior part of the inferior parietal lobule; integrates visual, auditory and somatosensory information for reading, writing and calculation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Arches over the posterior end of the superior temporal sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Supramarginal gyrus in front, occipital lobe behind, intraparietal sulcus above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (artery to the angular gyrus)

cards.pearl: Gerstmann syndrome (dominant angular gyrus): agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia and left-right disorientation.

cards.name: Precuneus
cards.function: Medial surface of the parietal lobe; association cortex for visuospatial imagery, episodic memory and self-awareness.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface between the marginal sulcus in front and the parieto-occipital sulcus behind; bounded below by the subparietal sulcus above the cingulate gyrus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Paracentral lobule in front, cuneus behind, isthmus of the cingulate gyrus below

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (pericallosal artery) and posterior cerebral artery

cards.pearl: Hypometabolism of the precuneus and posterior cingulate cortex on FDG-PET is an early finding in Alzheimer disease.

cards.name: Cingulate gyrus
cards.function: Limbic gyrus arching over the corpus callosum; involved in emotion, motivation, attention and the affective component of pain.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the hemisphere between the sulcus of the corpus callosum below and the cingulate sulcus above

details.label: Parts
details.value: Begins below the rostrum at the subcallosal area, arches around the genu and trunk, and narrows behind the splenium as the isthmus of the cingulate gyrus, continuous with the parahippocampal gyrus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (pericallosal and callosomarginal arteries)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Corpus callosum below; medial frontal gyrus, paracentral lobule and precuneus above; lies beneath the free edge of the falx cerebri

cards.pearl: Subfalcine herniation pushes the cingulate gyrus under the falx cerebri and can compress the anterior cerebral artery, causing contralateral leg weakness.

cards.name: Cingulate sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus on the medial surface that separates the cingulate gyrus from the medial frontal gyrus and paracentral lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs parallel to the corpus callosum above the cingulate gyrus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Gives off the paracentral sulcus in front of the paracentral lobule and ends by turning upward as the marginal sulcus behind it

details.label: Relations
details.value: The marginal sulcus lies just behind the upper end of the central sulcus; the callosomarginal artery runs in the cingulate sulcus

cards.pearl: The marginal sulcus is a reliable landmark for finding the central sulcus on sagittal and axial MRI.

cards.name: Parietooccipital sulcus
cards.function: Deep sulcus separating the parietal lobe (precuneus) from the occipital lobe (cuneus).

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the hemisphere, running downward and forward from the superior margin to meet the calcarine sulcus; only its upper end reaches the lateral surface

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precuneus in front, cuneus behind; a branch of the posterior cerebral artery runs in it

cards.name: Temporal lobe
cards.function: Lobe below the lateral sulcus containing auditory cortex, the sensory speech area (dominant side), visual association cortex and the medial temporal limbic structures for memory.

details.label: Location
details.value: Middle cranial fossa and upper surface of the tentorium cerebelli, below the lateral sulcus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri laterally; lateral occipitotemporal gyrus, medial occipitotemporal gyrus, parahippocampal gyrus and uncus inferomedially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (lateral surface and pole) and posterior cerebral artery (inferior and medial surface)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Temporal (inferior) horn of the lateral ventricle, hippocampus and amygdaloid body lie within it; temporal operculum covers the insula

cards.pearl: Temporal lobe lesions cause contralateral superior quadrantanopia; herpes simplex encephalitis and mesial temporal sclerosis preferentially involve this lobe.

cards.name: Temporal pole
cards.function: Anterior end of the temporal lobe; association cortex linked to the amygdaloid body and orbitofrontal cortex for semantic memory and emotion.

details.label: Location
details.value: Front of the middle cranial fossa, behind the greater wing of the sphenoid, below the stem of the lateral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior, middle and inferior temporal gyri converge on it; uncus and amygdaloid body lie posteromedially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (anterior temporal branches)

cards.pearl: A common site of traumatic contusion against the sphenoid; atrophy of the temporal pole is typical of semantic-variant frontotemporal dementia.

cards.name: Superior temporal gyrus
cards.function: Contains the primary auditory cortex on its upper surface and, posteriorly in the dominant hemisphere, the sensory speech area (of Wernicke).

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the temporal lobe between the lateral sulcus above and the superior temporal sulcus below

details.label: Parts
details.value: Its upper surface forms the temporal operculum and bears the transverse temporal gyri and temporal plane

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery, inferior division (temporal branches)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Insula deep to it; supramarginal and angular gyri cap its posterior end

cards.pearl: Wernicke (fluent, receptive) aphasia: fluent but meaningless speech with poor comprehension and repetition, from an inferior-division middle cerebral artery stroke.

cards.name: Transverse temporal gyri (of Heschl)
cards.function: Primary auditory cortex; receives the acoustic radiation from the medial geniculate body with a tonotopic arrangement and bilateral representation of each ear.

details.label: Location
details.value: Upper surface of the superior temporal gyrus, hidden in the floor of the lateral sulcus, running obliquely toward the insula

details.label: Parts
details.value: One or two transverse gyri; the flat temporal plane (auditory association cortex) lies behind them

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (temporal branches)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Insula medially; parietal operculum above

cards.pearl: Because each ear projects to both hemispheres, a unilateral cortical lesion does not cause deafness; the temporal plane is larger on the language-dominant side.

cards.name: Superior temporal sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that separates the superior and middle temporal gyri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the temporal lobe, parallel to the lateral sulcus; its posterior end turns up into the angular gyrus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior temporal gyrus above, middle temporal gyrus below

cards.name: Middle temporal gyrus
cards.function: Temporal association cortex concerned with language semantics and, posteriorly, visual motion processing.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the temporal lobe between the superior and inferior temporal sulci

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior temporal gyrus above, inferior temporal gyrus below; temporal (inferior) horn of the lateral ventricle deep to it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery (temporal branches)

cards.name: Inferior temporal sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus that separates the middle and inferior temporal gyri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lower lateral surface of the temporal lobe, often broken into segments

details.label: Relations
details.value: Middle temporal gyrus above, inferior temporal gyrus below

cards.name: Inferior temporal gyrus
cards.function: Visual association cortex of the ventral ("what") stream, concerned with recognition of objects and forms.

details.label: Location
details.value: Along the inferolateral margin of the temporal lobe, below the inferior temporal sulcus, extending onto the inferior surface as far as the occipitotemporal sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Middle temporal gyrus above; lateral occipitotemporal gyrus medially; rests on the floor of the middle cranial fossa and the tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle cerebral artery laterally and temporal branches of the posterior cerebral artery inferiorly

cards.name: Occipitotemporal sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus on the inferior surface of the hemisphere that separates the inferior temporal gyrus from the lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes, lateral and parallel to the collateral sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior temporal gyrus laterally, lateral occipitotemporal gyrus medially

cards.name: Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus
cards.function: The fusiform gyrus: ventral-stream visual association cortex specialized for recognition of faces, words and colors.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes between the occipitotemporal sulcus laterally and the collateral sulcus medially

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior temporal gyrus laterally; parahippocampal gyrus and medial occipitotemporal gyrus medially; rests on the tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (temporal branches)

cards.pearl: Bilateral (or right) fusiform lesions from posterior cerebral artery infarction cause prosopagnosia; dominant-side lesions cause alexia.

cards.name: Collateral sulcus
cards.function: Long sulcus on the inferior surface separating the parahippocampal and medial occipitotemporal gyri from the lateral occipitotemporal gyrus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the temporal and occipital lobes; continuous in front with, or just behind, the rhinal sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its depth raises the collateral eminence in the floor of the temporal (inferior) horn and the collateral trigone in the atrium of the lateral ventricle

cards.name: Parahippocampal gyrus
cards.function: Limbic gyrus on the medial edge of the temporal lobe; its entorhinal cortex is the main gateway of cortical input to the hippocampus for memory formation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferomedial temporal lobe between the collateral and rhinal sulci laterally and the hippocampal sulcus medially

details.label: Parts
details.value: Hooks back anteriorly as the uncus; continuous posteriorly with the isthmus of the cingulate gyrus above and the medial occipitotemporal gyrus (lingual gyrus) below

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (temporal branches) and anterior choroidal artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hippocampus and dentate gyrus lie above it in the temporal (inferior) horn; cerebral peduncle and free edge of the tentorium cerebelli medially

cards.pearl: Entorhinal cortex is the earliest site of neurofibrillary tangles in Alzheimer disease, explaining early loss of new memory.

cards.name: Uncus
cards.function: Hook-shaped anterior end of the parahippocampal gyrus; primary olfactory cortex overlying the amygdaloid body.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the anterior temporal lobe, behind the rhinal sulcus, projecting toward the tentorial notch

details.label: Relations
details.value: Amygdaloid body deep to it; oculomotor nerve (CN III), posterior cerebral artery and cerebral crus lie medially; optic tract above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery and posterior cerebral artery

cards.pearl: Uncal (transtentorial) herniation compresses CN III (ipsilateral blown pupil, then "down and out" eye), the cerebral crus (hemiparesis) and the posterior cerebral artery (hemianopia). Uncinate seizures begin with an olfactory aura.

cards.name: Occipital lobe
cards.function: Visual lobe: primary visual cortex along the calcarine sulcus with surrounding visual association cortex on the lateral occipital gyri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior end of the hemisphere, above the tentorium cerebelli, behind the parieto-occipital sulcus and a line to the preoccipital notch

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Cuneus and lingual gyrus on the medial surface; superior, middle (lateral) and inferior occipital gyri on the lateral surface, marked by the inconstant lunate and transverse occipital sulci; occipital pole

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery; the occipital pole also receives middle cerebral artery branches

details.label: Relations
details.value: Occipital (posterior) horn of the lateral ventricle and optic radiation lie within it; straight sinus and tentorium cerebelli below

cards.pearl: Posterior cerebral artery infarct: contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. Bilateral occipital infarction causes cortical blindness with preserved pupillary reflexes (Anton syndrome if the patient denies it).

cards.name: Occipital pole
cards.function: Posterior tip of the hemisphere; contains the part of primary visual cortex that represents the macula.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior end of the occipital lobe, where the calcarine sulcus reaches the lateral surface

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery with collateral supply from the middle cerebral artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Confluence of sinuses and internal occipital protuberance behind; lunate sulcus (inconstant) in front on the lateral surface

cards.pearl: Dual blood supply of the pole explains macular sparing in posterior cerebral artery strokes.

cards.name: Lunate and transverse occipital sulci
cards.function: Small, variable sulci on the lateral surface of the occipital lobe that separate the lateral occipital gyri (visual association cortex).

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the occipital lobe: transverse occipital sulcus behind the upper end of the parieto-occipital sulcus, continuous with the intraparietal sulcus; lunate sulcus (inconstant) just in front of the occipital pole

details.label: Relations
details.value: An anterior occipital sulcus, when present, runs up from the preoccipital notch and marks the border with the temporal lobe

cards.name: Calcarine sulcus
cards.function: Sulcus whose banks contain the primary visual (striate) cortex, where the optic radiation ends in a retinotopic map of the contralateral visual field.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the occipital lobe, from below the splenium of the corpus callosum to the occipital pole; joined by the parieto-occipital sulcus

details.label: Function
details.value: Upper bank (cuneus) receives the lower visual field, lower bank (lingual gyrus) the upper visual field; the macula is represented most posteriorly

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (medial occipital artery, calcarine branch)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its depth raises the calcar avis in the medial wall of the occipital (posterior) horn of the lateral ventricle

cards.pearl: Lesion of one bank gives a contralateral quadrantanopia: lingual gyrus - upper quadrant, cuneus - lower quadrant.

cards.name: Cuneus
cards.function: Wedge of medial occipital cortex forming the upper bank of the calcarine sulcus; primary and association visual cortex for the contralateral lower visual field.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial surface of the occipital lobe between the parieto-occipital sulcus in front and above and the calcarine sulcus below

details.label: Relations
details.value: Precuneus in front, lingual gyrus below; falx cerebri medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (medial occipital artery)

cards.pearl: A cuneus lesion produces a contralateral inferior homonymous quadrantanopia.

cards.name: Lingual gyrus
cards.function: Forms the lower bank of the calcarine sulcus; primary and association visual cortex for the contralateral upper visual field.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial and inferior surface of the occipital lobe between the calcarine sulcus above and the collateral sulcus below

details.label: Relations
details.value: Continuous in front with the parahippocampal gyrus as the medial occipitotemporal gyrus; cuneus above; rests on the tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (medial occipital artery)

cards.pearl: A lingual gyrus lesion produces a contralateral superior homonymous quadrantanopia; bilateral inferior occipital lesions cause achromatopsia.

cards.name: Longitudinal cerebral fissure
cards.function: Midline cleft that separates the two cerebral hemispheres and lodges the falx cerebri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Median plane from the frontal poles to the occipital poles; its floor centrally is the corpus callosum

details.label: Relations
details.value: Contains the falx cerebri with the superior and inferior sagittal sinuses, and the anterior cerebral arteries

cards.pearl: Blood layering in the fissure (interhemispheric) suggests an anterior communicating artery aneurysm or, in infants, abusive head trauma.

cards.name: Cerebral white matter
cards.function: Core of myelinated fibers beneath the cortex, made up of association fibers (within a hemisphere), commissural fibers (between hemispheres) and projection fibers (to and from subcortical centers).

details.label: Location
details.value: Fills the hemisphere between the cortex, the basal nuclei and the lateral ventricle

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Commissural fibers: corpus callosum, anterior commissure, commissure of fornix. Projection fibers: internal capsule, fornix, optic radiation. Association fibers: short fibers between gyri and long fasciculi between lobes

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Long penetrating medullary branches of the anterior, middle and posterior cerebral arteries; deep parts from lenticulostriate arteries

cards.pearl: Periventricular white matter is the typical site of multiple sclerosis plaques (ovoid lesions perpendicular to the ventricles) and of chronic small-vessel ischemic change.

cards.name: Corpus callosum
cards.function: Largest commissure of the brain, connecting corresponding cortical areas of the two hemispheres.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor of the longitudinal cerebral fissure; forms the roof of the lateral ventricles

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Rostrum, genu, trunk and splenium

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery (pericallosal artery); splenium from the posterior cerebral artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus of the corpus callosum above; septum pellucidum and fornix below; great cerebral vein (of Galen) curves around the splenium

cards.pearl: A left posterior cerebral artery infarct involving the splenium and left visual cortex causes alexia without agraphia; callosotomy is used for refractory drop attacks.

cards.name: Anterior commissure
cards.function: Small compact commissure connecting the temporal lobes and olfactory structures of the two sides.

details.label: Location
details.value: Crosses the midline in the upper part of the lamina terminalis, just in front of the columns of the fornix

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior wall of the 3rd ventricle; interventricular foramen (of Monro) behind and above; rostrum of the corpus callosum and subcallosal area in front

details.label: Function
details.value: Interconnects the middle and inferior temporal gyri, amygdaloid bodies and olfactory bulbs

cards.pearl: The anterior commissure-posterior commissure line is the standard reference plane for axial brain imaging and stereotactic surgery.

cards.name: Septum pellucidum
cards.function: Thin vertical double membrane that separates the frontal (anterior) horns and central parts of the two lateral ventricles.

details.label: Location
details.value: Median plane, stretched between the corpus callosum (genu, rostrum and trunk) above and in front and the fornix below and behind

details.label: Parts
details.value: Two laminae that may enclose a cavity, the cavum septum pellucidum

details.label: Relations
details.value: Head of the caudate nucleus lateral to it across the ventricle; septal nuclei lie at its base in front of the anterior commissure

cards.pearl: Absent septum pellucidum with optic nerve hypoplasia and pituitary deficiency is septo-optic dysplasia; a cavum septum pellucidum is common in the newborn and in boxers with chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

cards.name: Septal nuclei
cards.function: Limbic nuclei of the basal forebrain connected with the hippocampus (via the fornix), hypothalamus and habenula; part of the reward circuitry and a source of cholinergic input to the hippocampus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Deep to the subcallosal area on the medial surface, below the rostrum of the corpus callosum and in front of the lamina terminalis and anterior commissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Septum pellucidum above; columns of the fornix behind; stria medullaris of thalamus carries their fibers to the habenula; medial olfactory stria ends here

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral and anterior communicating arteries

cards.name: Fornix
cards.function: C-shaped fiber bundle that is the main output of the hippocampus, running to the mammillary bodies, septal nuclei and anterior thalamus (circuit of Papez) for memory consolidation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Arches from the hippocampus under the splenium and trunk of the corpus callosum, over the thalamus, then down in front of the interventricular foramen (of Monro) to the mammillary body

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Fimbria of hippocampus, crus, commissure of fornix, body and column

details.label: Relations
details.value: Septum pellucidum attaches to its upper surface; tela choroidea and choroid plexus of the 3rd ventricle lie below the body; the column forms the anterior boundary of the interventricular foramen

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior cerebral artery branches and posterior choroidal arteries

cards.pearl: Bilateral fornix damage (colloid cyst surgery, tumor) produces anterograde amnesia resembling hippocampal injury.

cards.name: Commissure of fornix
cards.function: Thin sheet of crossing fibers (hippocampal commissure) that connects the two hippocampi between the crura of the fornix.

details.label: Location
details.value: Under the splenium of the corpus callosum, spanning the two crura of the fornix where they converge to form the body

details.label: Relations
details.value: Splenium above; tela choroidea of the 3rd ventricle and pineal gland below

cards.name: Hippocampus
cards.function: Curved ridge of archicortex in the medial temporal lobe that is essential for forming new declarative (episodic) memories and for spatial memory.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor and medial wall of the temporal (inferior) horn of the lateral ventricle, above the parahippocampal gyrus

details.label: Parts
details.value: Pes of hippocampus (expanded anterior end), alveus (white matter on its ventricular surface), fimbria of hippocampus (becomes the crus of the fornix), dentate gyrus along its medial edge beside the hippocampal sulcus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (temporal branches) and anterior choroidal artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Amygdaloid body in front; choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle above; tail of the caudate nucleus and stria terminalis in the roof of the horn

cards.pearl: Hippocampal pyramidal cells are highly vulnerable to global hypoxia; bilateral damage causes anterograde amnesia, and hippocampal (mesial temporal) sclerosis is the commonest cause of refractory temporal lobe epilepsy.

cards.name: Dentate gyrus
cards.function: Narrow notched strip of archicortex that receives entorhinal input and relays it into the hippocampus; a site of adult neurogenesis.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial edge of the hippocampus, between the fimbria of hippocampus above and the parahippocampal gyrus below, in the depth of the hippocampal sulcus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Fimbria of hippocampus above; parahippocampal gyrus below; temporal (inferior) horn of the lateral ventricle laterally

cards.name: Amygdaloid body
cards.function: Almond-shaped limbic nuclear complex that attaches emotional significance, especially fear, to sensory stimuli and drives autonomic and endocrine responses through the hypothalamus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior temporal lobe deep to the uncus, at the tip of the temporal (inferior) horn of the lateral ventricle, just in front of the pes of hippocampus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Continuous with the tail of the caudate nucleus; stria terminalis leaves it and follows the caudate nucleus to the hypothalamus and septal area; lentiform nucleus above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery

cards.pearl: Bilateral amygdaloid damage (e.g., herpes simplex encephalitis) causes Kluver-Bucy syndrome: placidity, hyperorality, hypersexuality and visual agnosia.

cards.name: Stria terminalis
cards.function: Slender efferent bundle of the amygdaloid body that carries its output to the hypothalamus and septal area.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs with the tail and body of the caudate nucleus in the groove between the caudate nucleus and thalamus, in the roof of the temporal (inferior) horn and floor of the central part of the lateral ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior thalamostriate vein accompanies it; lamina affixa and thalamus medial to it; ends near the interventricular foramen (of Monro) and anterior commissure

cards.name: Basal nuclei (ganglia)
cards.function: Subcortical gray masses that modulate cortical motor output through the thalamus, facilitating wanted movement (direct pathway) and suppressing unwanted movement (indirect pathway).

details.label: Location
details.value: Deep in the cerebral hemisphere, lateral to the thalamus and lateral ventricle, split by the internal capsule

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Caudate nucleus, putamen and globus pallidus. Striatum = caudate nucleus + putamen; lentiform nucleus = putamen + globus pallidus; corpus striatum = all three

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral), recurrent artery of Heubner (anterior cerebral) and anterior choroidal artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Functionally linked with the substantia nigra and subthalamic nucleus; claustrum, external capsule and extreme capsule lie between the putamen and the insula

cards.pearl: Basal nuclei disease causes movement disorders without weakness: parkinsonism (substantia nigra), chorea (striatum), hemiballismus (subthalamic nucleus). Bilateral globus pallidus necrosis follows carbon monoxide poisoning.

cards.name: Caudate nucleus
cards.function: C-shaped part of the striatum that follows the lateral ventricle; input nucleus of the basal nuclei for cognitive and oculomotor loops.

details.label: Location
details.value: Bulges into the lateral wall of the lateral ventricle throughout its curve

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Head (in the lateral wall of the frontal horn), body (floor of the central part) and tail (roof of the temporal horn, ending at the amygdaloid body)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Recurrent artery of Heubner (anterior cerebral) and lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior limb of the internal capsule separates the head from the lentiform nucleus; thalamus medial to the body, with the stria terminalis and superior thalamostriate vein in the groove between them

cards.pearl: Huntington disease (CAG repeats, autosomal dominant): atrophy of the head of the caudate nucleus enlarges the frontal horns ("boxcar ventricles"), with chorea, dementia and psychiatric change.

cards.name: Lentiform nucleus
cards.function: Lens-shaped nuclear mass made up of the putamen laterally and the globus pallidus medially.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral to the internal capsule, medial to the external capsule, deep to the insula

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Putamen and globus pallidus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral artery); anterior choroidal artery to the medial globus pallidus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior limb of the internal capsule separates it from the head of the caudate nucleus, posterior limb from the thalamus; external capsule, claustrum, extreme capsule and insula lateral

cards.pearl: Wilson disease (hepatolenticular degeneration): copper deposition in the lentiform nuclei causes dystonia, tremor and psychiatric symptoms with Kayser-Fleischer rings.

cards.name: Putamen
cards.function: Lateral part of the lentiform nucleus and, with the caudate nucleus, the striatum; main input nucleus of the motor loop of the basal nuclei.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the external capsule laterally and the globus pallidus medially, deep to the insula

details.label: Function
details.value: Receives motor and somatosensory cortex and dopaminergic input from the substantia nigra; projects to the globus pallidus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral artery)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Joined to the head of the caudate nucleus by gray bridges across the anterior limb of the internal capsule; claustrum lateral

cards.pearl: The putamen is the most common site of hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (ruptured lenticulostriate microaneurysms), with contralateral hemiparesis from the adjacent internal capsule.

cards.name: Globus pallidus
cards.function: Medial, paler part of the lentiform nucleus; its medial segment is the main inhibitory (GABA) output of the basal nuclei to the thalamus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial to the putamen, lateral to the posterior limb and genu of the internal capsule

details.label: Parts
details.value: Lateral (external) and medial (internal) segments

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral) and anterior choroidal artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Putamen laterally; internal capsule and thalamus medially; anterior commissure and optic tract below

cards.pearl: Bilateral globus pallidus necrosis is typical of carbon monoxide poisoning; the medial segment is a deep brain stimulation target in Parkinson disease and dystonia.

cards.name: Claustrum, external capsule and extreme capsule
cards.function: Thin sheet of gray matter (claustrum) between two thin white-matter laminae, lying between the putamen and the insular cortex.

details.label: Location
details.value: From medial to lateral: putamen, external capsule, claustrum, extreme capsule, insula

details.label: Function
details.value: The claustrum is reciprocally connected with most of the cerebral cortex; the capsules carry association fibers

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate and insular branches of the middle cerebral artery

cards.name: Internal capsule
cards.function: Compact band of projection fibers connecting the cerebral cortex with the thalamus, brain stem and spinal cord; carries the corticospinal and corticonuclear tracts and thalamocortical radiations.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the lentiform nucleus laterally and the caudate nucleus and thalamus medially; continuous below with the cerebral crus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior limb (between head of caudate nucleus and lentiform nucleus), genu, posterior limb (between thalamus and lentiform nucleus) and retrolenticular part

details.label: Function
details.value: Genu: corticonuclear fibers. Posterior limb: corticospinal tract and somatosensory radiation. Retrolenticular part: optic radiation

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral); anterior choroidal artery to the lower posterior limb; recurrent artery of Heubner to the anterior limb

cards.pearl: A lacunar infarct of the posterior limb causes pure motor hemiparesis affecting face, arm and leg equally, without cortical signs.

cards.name: Optic radiation
cards.function: Geniculocalcarine projection carrying visual information from the lateral geniculate body to the primary visual cortex around the calcarine sulcus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Leaves the lateral geniculate body through the retrolenticular part of the internal capsule and sweeps around the lateral ventricle to the occipital lobe

details.label: Parts
details.value: Lower fibers loop forward over the temporal (inferior) horn (Meyer loop) and carry the upper visual field; upper fibers run directly back through the parietal lobe and carry the lower visual field

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery proximally, middle cerebral artery in the temporal and parietal white matter, posterior cerebral artery near the cortex

cards.pearl: Temporal lobe lesion: contralateral superior quadrantanopia ("pie in the sky"); parietal lesion: contralateral inferior quadrantanopia.

cards.name: Anterior perforated substance
cards.function: Area at the base of the forebrain pierced by the lenticulostriate arteries on their way to the basal nuclei and internal capsule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the brain, behind the division of the olfactory tract and lateral to the optic chiasm and optic tract

details.label: Relations
details.value: Uncus laterally; stem of the lateral sulcus with the middle cerebral artery below it; anterior cerebral artery crosses its medial part

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Pierced by lenticulostriate arteries (middle cerebral) and the recurrent artery of Heubner (anterior cerebral)

cards.name: Thalamus
cards.function: Paired ovoid nuclear mass that relays all sensory pathways except smell, plus cerebellar and basal nuclei output, to the cerebral cortex; also regulates arousal.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral wall of the 3rd ventricle above the hypothalamic sulcus; floor of the central part of the lateral ventricle; medial to the posterior limb of the internal capsule

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior, medial and lateral cell masses separated by the internal medullary lamina. Nuclei: ventral anterior, ventral lateral, ventral posterolateral, ventral posteromedial, medial dorsal, lateral dorsal, lateral posterior, centromedian and other intralaminar nuclei, median nuclei, reticular nuclei, pulvinar

details.label: Function
details.value: Ventral posterolateral - body sensation; ventral posteromedial - face sensation and taste; ventral lateral and ventral anterior - motor (cerebellum, basal nuclei); lateral geniculate - vision; medial geniculate - hearing; anterior and medial dorsal - limbic

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (thalamoperforating, thalamogeniculate and posterior choroidal arteries) and posterior communicating artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Joined to its fellow by the interthalamic adhesion; stria medullaris of thalamus along its upper medial edge; stria terminalis and caudate nucleus laterally; fornix and choroid plexus above

cards.pearl: A lacunar infarct of the ventral posterior nuclei causes pure contralateral hemisensory loss, sometimes followed by thalamic pain syndrome (Dejerine-Roussy). The thalamus is the second most common site of hypertensive hemorrhage.

cards.name: Pulvinar
cards.function: Large posterior nucleus of the thalamus connected with parietal, occipital and temporal association cortex; involved in visual attention.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior pole of the thalamus, overhanging the superior colliculus and the geniculate bodies

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral geniculate body and medial geniculate body below it; pineal gland and habenular trigone medially; crus of the fornix above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior choroidal and thalamogeniculate arteries (posterior cerebral artery)

cards.pearl: Symmetric pulvinar hyperintensity on MRI (the "pulvinar sign") is characteristic of variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

cards.name: Lateral geniculate body
cards.function: Thalamic relay for vision: receives the optic tract and projects through the optic radiation to the primary visual cortex.

details.label: Location
details.value: Under the pulvinar at the end of the optic tract, lateral to the medial geniculate body

details.label: Function
details.value: Six-layered dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus with a retinotopic map of the contralateral visual field; crossed and uncrossed fibers end in separate layers

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery and posterior choroidal arteries (posterior cerebral)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connected to the superior colliculus by the brachium of the superior colliculus; optic radiation leaves it through the retrolenticular part of the internal capsule

cards.pearl: Lesions behind the chiasm (optic tract, lateral geniculate body, radiation) cause contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

cards.name: Medial geniculate body
cards.function: Thalamic relay for hearing: receives the brachium of the inferior colliculus and projects through the acoustic radiation to the transverse temporal gyri.

details.label: Location
details.value: Under the pulvinar on the posterior surface of the thalamus, medial to the lateral geniculate body and lateral to the superior colliculus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Brachium of the inferior colliculus enters it; cerebral crus in front

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Thalamogeniculate arteries (posterior cerebral artery)

cards.pearl: Because auditory pathways are bilateral above the cochlear nuclei, a unilateral lesion here does not cause deafness.

cards.name: Optic tract
cards.function: Continuation of the visual pathway from the optic chiasm to the lateral geniculate body, carrying fibers from the ipsilateral temporal retina and contralateral nasal retina (the contralateral visual field).

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs back and laterally from the optic chiasm, around the cerebral crus, to the lateral geniculate body

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tuber cinereum and anterior perforated substance medially and above; uncus and parahippocampal gyrus laterally; some fibers continue through the brachium of the superior colliculus to the pretectal area for the light reflex

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery and posterior communicating artery

cards.pearl: An optic tract lesion causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia, typically incongruous, with a relative afferent pupillary defect in the contralateral eye.

cards.name: Habenula
cards.function: Small epithalamic nucleus at the posterior end of the stria medullaris of thalamus; relays limbic input from the septal nuclei and hypothalamus to the midbrain.

details.label: Location
details.value: Habenular trigone, on the dorsomedial thalamus just in front of the pineal gland and above the posterior commissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: The two habenulae are joined by the habenular commissure in the upper lamina of the pineal stalk; pulvinar laterally; 3rd ventricle medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior choroidal arteries (posterior cerebral artery)

cards.name: Stria medullaris of thalamus
cards.function: Fiber bundle carrying septal and hypothalamic afferents back to the habenula.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs along the junction of the superior and medial surfaces of the thalamus, from near the interventricular foramen (of Monro) to the habenular trigone

details.label: Relations
details.value: The tela choroidea of the 3rd ventricle attaches along it; choroid plexus of the 3rd ventricle medially

cards.name: Posterior commissure
cards.function: Small commissure at the junction of the diencephalon and midbrain; carries crossing fibers of the pretectal area that make the pupillary light reflex consensual.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lower lamina of the pineal stalk, above the opening of the cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius) into the 3rd ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Habenular commissure and pineal recess above; superior colliculus and tectal plate behind

details.label: Function
details.value: Interconnects the pretectal areas and nuclei controlling vertical gaze

cards.pearl: A pineal region mass compressing the posterior commissure and pretectal area causes Parinaud syndrome: upgaze palsy, light-near dissociation and convergence-retraction nystagmus.

cards.name: Pineal gland
cards.function: Midline endocrine gland that secretes melatonin in darkness, entraining circadian rhythm.

details.label: Location
details.value: Attached to the posterior wall of the 3rd ventricle by a stalk between the habenular commissure and posterior commissure; rests between the superior colliculi

details.label: Relations
details.value: Splenium of the corpus callosum and great cerebral vein (of Galen) above; tectal plate below; lies in the quadrigeminal cistern; pineal recess of the 3rd ventricle extends into its stalk

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior choroidal arteries (posterior cerebral artery)

cards.pearl: Pineal tumors (germinoma in adolescent boys) cause Parinaud syndrome and obstructive hydrocephalus by compressing the tectal plate and cerebral aqueduct; a calcified pineal is a normal midline marker on CT.

cards.name: Hypothalamus
cards.function: Master regulator of homeostasis: controls the pituitary gland, autonomic nervous system, temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep-wake cycle and emotional behavior.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor and lower lateral wall of the 3rd ventricle below the hypothalamic sulcus, from the lamina terminalis to the mammillary bodies

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Principal nuclei: paraventricular, supraoptic, dorsomedial, ventromedial, arcuate (infundibular), posterior, and mammillary body; surface parts are the optic chiasm, tuber cinereum with infundibulum, and mammillary bodies

details.label: Function
details.value: Supraoptic and paraventricular - vasopressin and oxytocin; arcuate - releasing hormones and dopamine; ventromedial - satiety; lateral area - hunger; anterior - cooling; posterior - heat conservation; suprachiasmatic - circadian rhythm

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Branches of the cerebral arterial circle (of Willis); superior hypophyseal arteries to the median eminence

details.label: Relations
details.value: Thalamus above; fornix runs through it to the mammillary body; hypophysis (pituitary gland) hangs from it by the infundibulum

cards.pearl: Craniopharyngioma or other suprasellar masses cause central diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism and bitemporal hemianopia; ventromedial damage causes hyperphagia and obesity.

cards.name: Tuber cinereum and median eminence
cards.function: Gray swelling of the hypothalamic floor from which the infundibulum arises; its median eminence is where releasing hormones enter the hypophyseal portal system.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor of the 3rd ventricle between the optic chiasm in front and the mammillary bodies behind

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic tracts on each side; infundibulum descends from it through the diaphragma sellae; arcuate (infundibular) nucleus lies in it; infundibular recess of the 3rd ventricle above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior hypophyseal arteries form the primary portal capillary plexus

cards.pearl: A hamartoma of the tuber cinereum causes gelastic (laughing) seizures and central precocious puberty.

cards.name: Mammillary bodies
cards.function: Paired hypothalamic nuclei that receive the fornix and project through the mammillothalamic tract to the anterior thalamus (circuit of Papez); needed for memory formation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the hypothalamus behind the tuber cinereum, in front of the posterior perforated substance in the interpeduncular fossa

details.label: Relations
details.value: Columns of the fornix end in them; mammillothalamic tract (of Vicq d'Azyr) ascends from them; cerebral crura on each side

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior communicating and posterior cerebral arteries

cards.pearl: Thiamine deficiency (alcohol use disorder, malnutrition) causes hemorrhagic necrosis of the mammillary bodies: Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia) and Korsakoff amnesia with confabulation.

cards.name: Hypophysis (pituitary gland)
cards.function: Master endocrine gland suspended from the hypothalamus by the infundibulum; the anterior lobe secretes six trophic hormones under portal control and the posterior lobe releases vasopressin and oxytocin.

details.label: Location
details.value: Hypophyseal fossa of the sella turcica, covered by the diaphragma sellae

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior lobe (adenohypophysis): pars distalis, pars tuberalis, pars intermedia. Posterior lobe (neurohypophysis): infundibular process, infundibular stem and median eminence of the tuber cinereum

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior hypophyseal arteries (internal carotid artery); hypophyseal portal veins link the median eminence to the anterior lobe

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic chiasm above; cavernous sinus and internal carotid artery on each side; sphenoidal sinus below and in front; anterior and posterior intercavernous sinuses around it

cards.pearl: A pituitary macroadenoma compresses the optic chiasm (bitemporal hemianopia); prolactinoma is the most common type. Pituitary surgery is done through the sphenoidal sinus.

cards.name: Anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) of pituitary gland
cards.function: Glandular lobe derived from oral ectoderm (Rathke pouch); secretes ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, GH and prolactin in response to hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior part of the hypophysis in the hypophyseal fossa

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Pars distalis (main part), pars tuberalis (wraps the infundibular stem) and pars intermedia (beside the cleft)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: No direct arterial supply of note: fed by hypophyseal portal veins from the primary plexus of the superior hypophyseal arteries

details.label: Relations
details.value: Separated from the posterior lobe by the cleft and pars intermedia

cards.pearl: Its low-pressure portal supply makes it vulnerable to infarction after postpartum hemorrhage (Sheehan syndrome): failure of lactation, amenorrhea, secondary adrenal insufficiency.

cards.name: Posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) of pituitary gland
cards.function: Neural lobe: a downgrowth of the hypothalamus that stores and releases vasopressin (ADH) and oxytocin made in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior part of the hypophysis, continuous above with the infundibulum and tuber cinereum

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Infundibular process (the lobe proper), infundibular stem and median eminence of the tuber cinereum

details.label: Function
details.value: Hormones travel down axons of the supraopticohypophyseal (hypothalamohypophyseal) tract and are released into capillaries

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Inferior hypophyseal arteries (internal carotid artery, cavernous segment)

cards.pearl: Damage to the stalk or supraoptic/paraventricular neurons causes central diabetes insipidus; the normal posterior lobe is a "bright spot" on T1 MRI that is lost in this condition.

cards.name: Lamina terminalis
cards.function: Thin plate forming the anterior wall of the 3rd ventricle; marks the rostral end of the embryonic neural tube and contains an osmoreceptive circumventricular organ.

details.label: Location
details.value: Stretches from the rostrum of the corpus callosum and anterior commissure down to the upper surface of the optic chiasm

details.label: Relations
details.value: Supraoptic recess of the 3rd ventricle behind its lower end; anterior cerebral and anterior communicating arteries in front; subcallosal area in front and above

cards.pearl: Surgical fenestration of the lamina terminalis is one route for diverting CSF in obstructive hydrocephalus.

cards.name: Lateral ventricle
cards.function: Paired C-shaped cavity of each cerebral hemisphere; its choroid plexus produces most of the cerebrospinal fluid, which drains through the interventricular foramen to the 3rd ventricle.

details.label: Location
details.value: Within the cerebral hemisphere, wrapping around the thalamus and caudate nucleus

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Frontal (anterior) horn, central part, occipital (posterior) horn and temporal (inferior) horn

details.label: Relations
details.value: Roof: corpus callosum. Medial wall: septum pellucidum and fornix. Lateral wall and floor: head and body of the caudate nucleus, thalamus. Temporal horn: hippocampus in the floor, tail of the caudate nucleus in the roof. Occipital horn: calcar avis medially

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Choroid plexus supplied by the anterior choroidal artery and posterior choroidal arteries

cards.pearl: Asymmetric dilation of one lateral ventricle points to obstruction at the interventricular foramen; in premature infants, germinal matrix hemorrhage ruptures into the lateral ventricle.

cards.name: Interventricular foramen (of Monro)
cards.function: Opening that drains each lateral ventricle into the 3rd ventricle.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the column of the fornix in front and the anterior tubercle of the thalamus behind

details.label: Relations
details.value: Choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle is continuous through it with that of the 3rd ventricle; superior thalamostriate vein joins the internal cerebral vein at its margin; anterior commissure in front and below

cards.pearl: A colloid cyst of the anterior 3rd ventricle can block both foramina, causing positional headache, acute hydrocephalus and sudden death.

cards.name: Third ventricle
cards.function: Narrow midline cavity of the diencephalon between the two thalami; receives CSF from the lateral ventricles and passes it to the cerebral aqueduct.

details.label: Location
details.value: Median cleft between the thalami and the halves of the hypothalamus

details.label: Parts
details.value: Recesses: supraoptic, infundibular, pineal and suprapineal; crossed by the interthalamic adhesion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior wall: lamina terminalis and anterior commissure. Floor: optic chiasm, tuber cinereum, mammillary bodies. Roof: tela choroidea with choroid plexus beneath the fornix. Posterior: pineal gland, habenular and posterior commissures

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Choroid plexus from the posterior choroidal arteries

cards.pearl: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy opens the floor in front of the mammillary bodies into the interpeduncular cistern to bypass aqueductal obstruction.

cards.name: Cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius)
cards.function: Narrow channel through the midbrain connecting the 3rd and 4th ventricles; the narrowest point of the CSF pathway.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midbrain, between the tectal plate behind and the tegmentum in front

details.label: Relations
details.value: Surrounded by periaqueductal gray matter; oculomotor and trochlear nuclei lie just ventral to it; posterior commissure at its upper opening; superior medullary velum at its lower end

cards.pearl: Aqueductal stenosis (congenital, or compression by a midbrain or pineal tumor) causes noncommunicating hydrocephalus with dilated lateral and 3rd ventricles and a normal 4th ventricle.

cards.name: Fourth ventricle
cards.function: Tent-shaped cavity of the hindbrain between the pons and medulla in front and the cerebellum behind; CSF leaves it for the subarachnoid space through the median and lateral apertures.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior to the pons and upper medulla oblongata, anterior to the cerebellum

details.label: Parts
details.value: Floor: rhomboid fossa. Roof: superior medullary velum and inferior medullary velum meeting at the fastigium. Lateral recesses extend around the inferior cerebellar peduncles

details.label: Relations
details.value: Continuous above with the cerebral aqueduct and below with the central canal of the spinal cord; nodule of the vermis and tonsils of the cerebellum behind

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle from the posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Childhood posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma of the vermis, ependymoma of the floor) fill the 4th ventricle, causing obstructive hydrocephalus with morning headache, vomiting and truncal ataxia.

cards.name: Rhomboid fossa of 4th ventricle
cards.function: Diamond-shaped floor of the 4th ventricle formed by the posterior surfaces of the pons and upper medulla; its elevations mark underlying cranial nerve nuclei.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the cerebellar peduncles, from the cerebral aqueduct above to the obex below

details.label: Parts
details.value: Posterior median sulcus, medial eminence with the facial colliculus, sulcus limitans with superior fovea and inferior fovea, locus coeruleus, vestibular area, striae medullares, hypoglossal trigone, vagal trigone, obex

details.label: Relations
details.value: Facial colliculus overlies the abducens nucleus and the genu of the facial nerve; hypoglossal trigone overlies the nucleus of the hypoglossal nerve; vagal trigone overlies the dorsal nucleus of the vagus nerve; vestibular area overlies the vestibular nuclei

cards.pearl: A lesion at the facial colliculus produces ipsilateral lateral gaze palsy with ipsilateral lower motor neuron facial palsy. The area postrema near the obex is the chemoreceptor trigger zone for vomiting.

cards.name: Median aperture (foramen of Magendie) and lateral apertures (foramina of Luschka)
cards.function: The three openings in the roof and lateral recesses of the 4th ventricle through which CSF passes from the ventricular system into the subarachnoid space.

details.label: Location
details.value: Median aperture: midline of the inferior medullary velum, opening into the posterior cerebellomedullary cistern. Lateral apertures: ends of the lateral recesses at the cerebellopontine angle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle protrudes through each lateral aperture beside the flocculus and the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves

cards.pearl: Failure of these apertures to open (Dandy-Walker malformation) gives a cystic 4th ventricle with vermis hypoplasia; scarring after meningitis or subarachnoid hemorrhage can also obstruct outflow.

cards.name: Choroid plexus
cards.function: Vascular fringes of pia mater covered by specialized ependyma that secrete cerebrospinal fluid (about 500 mL/day) and form the blood-CSF barrier.

details.label: Location
details.value: Central part and temporal (inferior) horn of each lateral ventricle, roof of the 3rd ventricle and roof of the 4th ventricle; absent from the frontal and occipital horns and the cerebral aqueduct

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Choroid plexus of lateral ventricle, choroid plexus of 3rd ventricle (continuous through the interventricular foramen) and choroid plexus of 4th ventricle (extends out of the lateral apertures)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior choroidal artery (internal carotid), posterior choroidal arteries (posterior cerebral) and posterior inferior cerebellar artery; drained by choroidal veins into the internal cerebral veins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Invaginates the ventricle along the tela choroidea; in the lateral ventricle it lies in the choroid fissure between the fornix and thalamus

cards.pearl: Calcified choroid plexus in the atria is a normal CT finding. Choroid plexus papilloma (children, lateral ventricle) causes hydrocephalus from CSF overproduction.

cards.name: Subarachnoid cisterns
cards.function: Enlargements of the subarachnoid space at the base of the brain where the arachnoid bridges over depressions; they hold pools of CSF and contain the major arteries and cranial nerve roots.

details.label: Location
details.value: Around the brain stem and base of the brain, between the arachnoid mater and pia mater

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Posterior cerebellomedullary cistern, prepontine cistern, interpeduncular cistern, chiasmatic cistern and quadrigeminal cistern (with the great cerebral vein of Galen)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Interpeduncular cistern holds the oculomotor nerves and the posterior part of the cerebral arterial circle; prepontine cistern holds the basilar artery; the median aperture opens into the posterior cerebellomedullary cistern

cards.pearl: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage fills the basal cisterns with blood on CT; effacement of the cisterns indicates raised intracranial pressure and impending herniation.

cards.name: Circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
