cards.function: CSF made by the choroid plexus flows through the ventricles into the subarachnoid space and is reabsorbed into the dural venous sinuses, cushioning the brain and clearing metabolites.

details.label: Parts
details.value: Lateral ventricle - interventricular foramen (of Monro) - 3rd ventricle - cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius) - 4th ventricle - median aperture and lateral apertures - subarachnoid space and cisterns - arachnoid granulations - superior sagittal sinus

details.label: Function
details.value: Total volume about 150 mL, turned over three to four times a day; a small amount enters the central canal of the spinal cord

details.label: Relations
details.value: The subarachnoid space continues around the spinal cord and along the meningeal sheath of the optic nerve

cards.pearl: Noncommunicating hydrocephalus = block within the ventricles; communicating = impaired absorption (after meningitis or subarachnoid hemorrhage). Normal pressure hydrocephalus: gait apraxia, urinary incontinence, dementia.

cards.name: Dura mater
cards.function: Tough outer meninx (pachymeninx) lining the skull; its two layers separate to enclose the dural venous sinuses and its inner layer folds inward as partitions that support the brain.

details.label: Location
details.value: Adherent to the inner surface of the calvaria and cranial base; continuous at the foramen magnum with the spinal dura mater

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Periosteal (endosteal) layer and meningeal layer. Dural folds: falx cerebri, tentorium cerebelli, falx cerebelli and diaphragma sellae

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle meningeal artery (frontal and parietal branches) chiefly; also accessory meningeal artery, anterior meningeal branch of the anterior ethmoidal artery, meningeal branches of the ascending pharyngeal, occipital and vertebral arteries, and the meningohypophyseal trunk

details.label: Relations
details.value: Innervated mainly by meningeal branches of the trigeminal nerve above the tentorium and by C2-C3 and the vagus nerve below it; arachnoid mater lies against its inner surface

cards.pearl: Epidural hematoma: torn middle meningeal artery at the pterion strips dura from bone - lens-shaped clot limited by sutures, lucid interval. Subdural hematoma: torn bridging veins - crescent-shaped clot that crosses sutures.

cards.name: Falx cerebri
cards.function: Sickle-shaped midline fold of meningeal dura mater in the longitudinal cerebral fissure that separates the cerebral hemispheres and limits side-to-side displacement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Attached in front to the crista galli and frontal crest, along the vault to the internal occipital protuberance, and behind to the upper surface of the tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus in its attached border, inferior sagittal sinus in its free border, straight sinus along its junction with the tentorium cerebelli; corpus callosum and cingulate gyri lie below the free edge

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior meningeal branch of the anterior ethmoidal artery and branches of the middle meningeal artery

cards.pearl: Subfalcine herniation: the cingulate gyrus is pushed under the free edge. A parasagittal (falcine) meningioma compresses the leg area and causes contralateral or bilateral leg weakness.

cards.name: Tentorium cerebelli
cards.function: Tent-like dural fold that roofs the posterior cranial fossa, separating the occipital lobes above from the cerebellum below.

details.label: Location
details.value: Attached to the posterior clinoid processes, superior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone and the grooves for the transverse sinuses on the occipital bone; anterior clinoid processes by its free border

details.label: Parts
details.value: Fixed (peripheral) border and free border; the free border surrounds the tentorial notch, which transmits the midbrain

details.label: Relations
details.value: Transverse sinus and superior petrosal sinus in its attached border; straight sinus along the attachment of the falx cerebri; occipital lobe, parahippocampal gyrus and uncus above; cerebellum below

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Tentorial artery (meningohypophyseal trunk) and meningeal branches of the vertebral and occipital arteries

cards.pearl: Uncal (transtentorial) herniation through the tentorial notch: ipsilateral dilated pupil (CN III), contralateral or ipsilateral hemiparesis (Kernohan notch), posterior cerebral artery infarction. Supratentorial dural pain refers to the forehead via CN V1.

cards.name: Falx cerebelli
cards.function: Small midline dural fold below the tentorium cerebelli that partly separates the cerebellar hemispheres.

details.label: Location
details.value: Attached to the internal occipital crest from the internal occipital protuberance toward the foramen magnum; projects into the posterior cerebellar notch

details.label: Relations
details.value: Contains the occipital sinus in its attached border; tentorium cerebelli above

cards.name: Diaphragma sellae
cards.function: Small circular dural fold that roofs the hypophyseal fossa and has a central opening for the infundibulum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Stretched between the tuberculum sellae and anterior clinoid processes in front and the dorsum sellae and posterior clinoid processes behind

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypophysis (pituitary gland) below; optic chiasm and chiasmatic cistern above; cavernous sinus and internal carotid artery on each side; anterior and posterior intercavernous sinuses in its margins

cards.pearl: A pituitary adenoma that expands through the opening becomes suprasellar and compresses the optic chiasm; an incompetent diaphragm lets arachnoid herniate into the fossa (empty sella).

cards.name: Arachnoid mater and subarachnoid space
cards.function: Thin avascular middle meninx held against the dura; the subarachnoid space beneath it contains CSF, the cerebral arteries and veins, and arachnoid trabeculae.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lines the inner surface of the dura mater and bridges over sulci and cisterns without dipping into them

details.label: Parts
details.value: Arachnoid mater, arachnoid trabeculae, subarachnoid space with its cisterns, arachnoid granulations

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subdural space is only a potential space between dura and arachnoid, crossed by the superior cerebral (bridging) veins; pia mater lies on the brain surface; arachnoid and pia together are the leptomeninges

cards.pearl: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (ruptured saccular aneurysm, trauma): thunderclap headache, blood in sulci and cisterns on CT, xanthochromia on lumbar puncture. Meningitis is inflammation of the leptomeninges and CSF.

cards.name: Arachnoid granulations
cards.function: Tufts of arachnoid that project through the meningeal dura into the venous sinuses and act as one-way valves returning CSF to venous blood.

details.label: Location
details.value: Along the superior sagittal sinus and in its lateral (venous) lacunae (of Trolard); fewer along other dural sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Indent the inner table of the calvaria as granular foveolae beside the sagittal suture; openings of the superior cerebral veins lie nearby

cards.pearl: Clogging of the granulations by blood or inflammatory debris (subarachnoid hemorrhage, meningitis) causes communicating hydrocephalus.

cards.name: Pia mater
cards.function: Delicate vascular inner meninx that adheres to the surface of the brain, following every gyrus and sulcus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Directly on the brain surface, deep to the subarachnoid space

details.label: Function
details.value: Carries small vessels into the brain surrounded by perivascular spaces; with ependyma forms the tela choroidea and choroid plexus of the ventricles

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cerebral arteries and veins lie on it in the subarachnoid space; fused with the glial limiting membrane of the cortex

cards.name: Midbrain
cards.function: Shortest part of the brain stem, connecting the pons to the diencephalon through the tentorial notch; contains the nuclei of CN III and IV, the substantia nigra and red nucleus, and centers for vertical gaze and pupillary reflexes.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the pons below and the thalamus above, traversed by the cerebral aqueduct (of Sylvius)

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Tectal plate (superior and inferior colliculi) behind the aqueduct; cerebral peduncles in front, each made of tegmentum, substantia nigra and cerebral crus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery, superior cerebellar artery and paramedian branches from the top of the basilar artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Oculomotor nerve (CN III) emerges in the interpeduncular fossa, trochlear nerve (CN IV) below the inferior colliculus; free border of the tentorium cerebelli, uncus and posterior cerebral artery lie alongside

cards.pearl: Weber syndrome (paramedian midbrain infarct): ipsilateral CN III palsy with contralateral hemiparesis. Dorsal midbrain compression gives Parinaud syndrome.

cards.name: Cerebral peduncle
cards.function: Each half of the midbrain in front of the cerebral aqueduct, connecting the cerebral hemisphere with the pons.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior to the tectal plate and cerebral aqueduct; the two peduncles diverge upward and bound the interpeduncular fossa

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Cerebral crus (anterior, descending cortical fibers), substantia nigra, and tegmentum (with the red nucleus and oculomotor nucleus)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery and posterior communicating artery branches

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic tract winds around its upper end; oculomotor nerve (CN III) emerges on its medial side; trochlear nerve (CN IV) and posterior cerebral artery curve around it

cards.pearl: In uncal herniation the opposite cerebral peduncle is pressed against the tentorial edge (Kernohan notch), giving hemiparesis on the same side as the mass - a false localizing sign.

cards.name: Cerebral crus
cards.function: Anterior part (base) of the cerebral peduncle: a thick band of descending corticospinal, corticonuclear and corticopontine fibers continuous with the internal capsule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior surface of the midbrain on each side of the interpeduncular fossa, in front of the substantia nigra

details.label: Function
details.value: Middle three-fifths carries corticospinal and corticonuclear fibers; medial and lateral fifths carry corticopontine fibers

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral and posterior communicating arteries; anterior choroidal artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic tract crosses its upper lateral surface; oculomotor nerve (CN III) emerges along its medial edge; continues into the basilar part of the pons

cards.pearl: A crus lesion gives contralateral hemiparesis including the lower face; with the adjacent CN III fascicles this is Weber syndrome.

cards.name: Interpeduncular fossa
cards.function: Depression between the two cerebral crura on the anterior surface of the midbrain, from which the oculomotor nerves emerge.

details.label: Location
details.value: Bounded by the cerebral crura laterally, the mammillary bodies in front and the upper border of the pons behind

details.label: Parts
details.value: Its floor is the posterior perforated substance, pierced by thalamoperforating branches of the posterior cerebral arteries

details.label: Relations
details.value: Roofed by arachnoid as the interpeduncular cistern, which contains the bifurcation of the basilar artery, posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries and the oculomotor nerves (CN III)

cards.pearl: CN III leaves the fossa between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, where a posterior communicating artery aneurysm compresses it: painful palsy with a dilated pupil.

cards.name: Superior colliculus
cards.function: Upper pair of elevations of the tectal plate; a visual reflex center that directs eye and head movements toward stimuli.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior surface of the upper midbrain, below the pineal gland and pulvinar

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connected to the lateral geniculate body and optic tract by the brachium of the superior colliculus; pretectal area and posterior commissure just above; oculomotor nucleus in the tegmentum at this level

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery and superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Pressure on the superior colliculi and pretectal area (pinealoma, hydrocephalus) causes paralysis of upward gaze - Parinaud syndrome, the "setting-sun" sign in infants.

cards.name: Inferior colliculus
cards.function: Lower pair of elevations of the tectal plate; obligatory relay of the ascending auditory pathway from the lateral lemniscus to the medial geniculate body.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior surface of the lower midbrain, below the superior colliculus and above the superior medullary velum

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connected to the medial geniculate body by the brachium of the inferior colliculus; trochlear nerve (CN IV) emerges just below it; trochlear nucleus in the tegmentum at this level

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: The trochlear nerve emerging below the inferior colliculus is the only cranial nerve to exit dorsally and to cross completely, so a nuclear lesion weakens the contralateral superior oblique.

cards.name: Red nucleus
cards.function: Large tegmental motor relay that receives cerebellar output through the superior cerebellar peduncle and cortical input, and projects to the inferior olivary complex and spinal cord (rubrospinal tract).

details.label: Location
details.value: Tegmentum of the upper midbrain at the level of the superior colliculus, behind the substantia nigra

details.label: Relations
details.value: Fascicles of the oculomotor nerve (CN III) pass through or beside it on the way to the interpeduncular fossa; decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncles lies just below

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Paramedian branches of the posterior cerebral and basilar arteries

cards.pearl: Benedikt syndrome: ipsilateral CN III palsy with contralateral tremor and ataxia. Lesions above the red nucleus give decorticate (flexor) posturing, below it decerebrate (extensor) posturing.

cards.name: Substantia nigra
cards.function: Pigmented midbrain nucleus whose compact part sends dopaminergic fibers to the striatum (nigrostriatal pathway) and whose reticular part is an output nucleus of the basal nuclei.

details.label: Location
details.value: Cerebral peduncle, between the cerebral crus in front and the tegmentum with the red nucleus behind

details.label: Parts
details.value: Compact part (dopaminergic, melanin-containing) and reticular part (GABAergic)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior cerebral artery (paramedian and short circumferential branches)

cards.pearl: Parkinson disease: loss of dopaminergic neurons of the compact part with Lewy bodies and depigmentation - resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and postural instability.

cards.name: Oculomotor nucleus and accessory oculomotor (Edinger-Westphal) nucleus
cards.function: Motor nuclei of CN III: the oculomotor nucleus supplies the superior, medial and inferior recti, inferior oblique and levator palpebrae superioris; the accessory nucleus supplies preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for pupillary constriction and accommodation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Tegmentum of the upper midbrain, ventral to the cerebral aqueduct at the level of the superior colliculus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Fibers run forward through the tegmentum and red nucleus to emerge in the interpeduncular fossa; medial longitudinal fasciculus lies alongside; accessory nucleus fibers synapse in the ciliary ganglion

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Paramedian branches of the basilar bifurcation and posterior cerebral arteries

cards.pearl: The accessory oculomotor nuclei of both sides receive input from each pretectal area, so light in one eye constricts both pupils (consensual reflex).

cards.name: Trochlear nucleus
cards.function: Motor nucleus of CN IV supplying the contralateral superior oblique muscle.

details.label: Location
details.value: Tegmentum of the lower midbrain, ventral to the cerebral aqueduct at the level of the inferior colliculus, just below the oculomotor nucleus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its fibers pass dorsally around the aqueduct, decussate in the superior medullary velum and emerge below the inferior colliculus; medial longitudinal fasciculus lies ventral to it

cards.pearl: CN IV palsy: vertical diplopia worse on downgaze and looking toward the nose (reading, stairs), with compensatory head tilt away from the affected eye.

cards.name: Pons
cards.function: Middle part of the brain stem; its basilar part relays cortical input to the cerebellum and carries the corticospinal tract, and its tegmentum contains the nuclei of CN V, VI, VII and VIII and the horizontal gaze center.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the midbrain and medulla oblongata, on the clivus, in front of the 4th ventricle and cerebellum

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Basilar (anterior) part with pontine nuclei and transverse fibers forming the middle cerebellar peduncles; tegmentum (posterior part) forming the upper half of the rhomboid fossa

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Pontine arteries of the basilar artery; anterior inferior cerebellar and superior cerebellar arteries laterally

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trigeminal nerve (CN V) emerges from its lateral surface; abducens (CN VI), facial (CN VII) and vestibulocochlear (CN VIII) nerves emerge at its lower border; basilar artery lies in the prepontine cistern in front

cards.pearl: Basilar occlusion infarcting the basilar pons causes locked-in syndrome (quadriplegia with preserved consciousness and vertical eye movements). Pontine hemorrhage: coma, pinpoint pupils. Rapid sodium correction causes osmotic demyelination here.

cards.name: Nuclei of trigeminal nerve
cards.function: One motor and three sensory nuclei of CN V, forming a column from the midbrain to the upper cervical cord.

details.label: Location
details.value: Motor and principal sensory nuclei in the mid-pons tegmentum; mesencephalic nucleus extends up beside the cerebral aqueduct; spinal nucleus descends through the medulla to C2

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Mesencephalic nucleus of trigeminal nerve, principal sensory nucleus of trigeminal nerve, spinal tract and spinal nucleus of trigeminal nerve, motor nucleus of trigeminal nerve

details.label: Function
details.value: Mesencephalic - proprioception from muscles of mastication (afferent limb of the jaw jerk); principal - fine touch of the face; spinal - pain and temperature of the face (also from CN VII, IX, X); motor - muscles of mastication

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Pontine arteries (basilar); posterior inferior cerebellar artery for the spinal nucleus in the medulla

cards.pearl: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome involves the spinal tract and nucleus: loss of pain and temperature on the ipsilateral face and contralateral body.

cards.name: Abducens nucleus
cards.function: Motor nucleus of CN VI for the lateral rectus; also contains interneurons that cross and ascend in the medial longitudinal fasciculus to the opposite medial rectus subnucleus, making it the center for conjugate horizontal gaze.

details.label: Location
details.value: Tegmentum of the lower pons beneath the facial colliculus in the floor of the 4th ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: The genu of the facial nerve loops around it; medial longitudinal fasciculus medially; its fibers run forward to emerge at the pontomedullary junction

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Paramedian pontine arteries (basilar artery)

cards.pearl: A nuclear lesion causes ipsilateral gaze palsy (neither eye can look to that side), usually with ipsilateral facial palsy, whereas a nerve lesion affects only abduction of one eye.

cards.name: Facial nucleus
cards.function: Branchial motor nucleus of CN VII supplying the muscles of facial expression, stapedius, stylohyoid and posterior belly of digastric.

details.label: Location
details.value: Ventrolateral tegmentum of the lower pons

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its fibers loop dorsally around the abducens nucleus as the genu of the facial nerve, raising the facial colliculus, then pass out at the cerebellopontine angle

details.label: Function
details.value: The part for the upper face receives corticonuclear fibers from both hemispheres; the part for the lower face from the opposite hemisphere only

cards.pearl: Upper motor neuron lesion (stroke): contralateral lower face weakness with forehead sparing. Lower motor neuron lesion (Bell palsy): whole ipsilateral half of the face.

cards.name: Superior salivatory nucleus
cards.function: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of the facial nerve (intermediate nerve) for the lacrimal, nasal, palatine, submandibular and sublingual glands.

details.label: Location
details.value: Tegmentum of the lower pons, near the facial nucleus

details.label: Function
details.value: Fibers travel in the greater petrosal nerve to the pterygopalatine ganglion (lacrimation, nasal and palatine glands) and in the chorda tympani to the submandibular ganglion (salivation)

cards.pearl: Aberrant regeneration after facial nerve injury can redirect salivatory fibers to the lacrimal gland, producing "crocodile tears" when eating.

cards.name: Inferior salivatory nucleus
cards.function: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of the glossopharyngeal nerve for the parotid gland.

details.label: Location
details.value: Upper medulla oblongata, just below the superior salivatory nucleus

details.label: Function
details.value: Fibers travel in the tympanic nerve and lesser petrosal nerve to the otic ganglion; postganglionic fibers reach the parotid gland with the auriculotemporal nerve

cards.pearl: After parotid surgery these secretomotor fibers may regrow into sweat glands of the overlying skin, causing gustatory sweating (Frey syndrome).

cards.name: Vestibular nuclei
cards.function: Four nuclei that receive the vestibular nerve and project to the spinal cord, cerebellum and extraocular motor nuclei to maintain balance and gaze stability (vestibulo-ocular reflex).

details.label: Location
details.value: Beneath the vestibular area in the lateral part of the rhomboid fossa, at the pontomedullary junction

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior, lateral, medial and inferior vestibular nuclei

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connect with CN III, IV and VI nuclei through the medial longitudinal fasciculus, with the flocculonodular lobe through the inferior cerebellar peduncle, and with the spinal cord through the vestibulospinal tracts

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery and anterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Lateral medullary infarction involves them: vertigo, nystagmus, nausea and falling toward the side of the lesion. Caloric testing (COWS) assesses this pathway in comatose patients.

cards.name: Cochlear nuclei
cards.function: First central relay of hearing: receive the cochlear nerve and project bilaterally through the trapezoid body and lateral lemniscus to the inferior colliculi.

details.label: Location
details.value: On the surface of the inferior cerebellar peduncle at the pontomedullary junction

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior and posterior cochlear nuclei

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Lesions of the cochlear nerve or nuclei cause ipsilateral deafness; lesions above them do not, because the pathway becomes bilateral.

cards.name: Medulla oblongata
cards.function: Lowest part of the brain stem, continuous with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum; contains the cardiovascular and respiratory centers and the nuclei of CN IX, X, XI and XII.

details.label: Location
details.value: From the lower border of the pons to the foramen magnum, on the basilar part of the occipital bone, in front of the cerebellum

details.label: Parts
details.value: Anterior: pyramids and decussation of pyramids. Lateral: olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle. Posterior: gracile and cuneate fasciculi and tubercles below, lower half of the rhomboid fossa above; central canal opens at the obex

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral arteries, anterior spinal artery (medial) and posterior inferior cerebellar artery (lateral)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) emerges between pyramid and olive; glossopharyngeal (CN IX), vagus (CN X) and accessory (CN XI) nerves emerge behind the olive; tonsils of the cerebellum lie posterolaterally

cards.pearl: Lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome from posterior inferior cerebellar or vertebral artery occlusion: dysphagia, hoarseness, vertigo, ipsilateral Horner syndrome and ataxia, crossed pain and temperature loss. Tonsillar herniation compresses the medulla and stops respiration.

cards.name: Pyramids and decussation of pyramids
cards.function: Paired anterior columns of the medulla formed by the corticospinal tracts; most fibers cross in the decussation of pyramids to become the lateral corticospinal tract.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior surface of the medulla oblongata on each side of the anterior median fissure; the decussation lies at the junction with the spinal cord

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olive lateral, separated by the groove from which the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) rootlets emerge; abducens nerve (CN VI) emerges at their upper end; vertebral arteries and anterior spinal artery lie in front

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior spinal artery and paramedian branches of the vertebral arteries

cards.pearl: Medial medullary syndrome (anterior spinal artery): contralateral hemiparesis sparing the face, contralateral loss of position and vibration sense, and ipsilateral tongue weakness. Lesions above the decussation give contralateral signs, below it ipsilateral.

cards.name: Olive
cards.function: Oval swelling on the lateral medulla produced by the inferior olivary complex, which sends climbing fibers to the opposite cerebellar hemisphere for motor learning and timing.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral surface of the upper medulla oblongata, behind the pyramid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) rootlets emerge in front of it; glossopharyngeal (CN IX), vagus (CN X) and accessory (CN XI) rootlets emerge behind it; inferior cerebellar peduncle posterolateral

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: A lesion in the dentate-red nucleus-olive triangle causes hypertrophic olivary degeneration with palatal myoclonus.

cards.name: Nucleus ambiguus
cards.function: Branchial motor nucleus for muscles of the pharynx, larynx and soft palate through CN IX, CN X and the cranial root of CN XI; also supplies cardioinhibitory vagal fibers.

details.label: Location
details.value: Ventrolateral reticular formation of the medulla oblongata, behind the inferior olivary complex

details.label: Function
details.value: Stylopharyngeus (CN IX); muscles of the palate, pharynx and larynx (CN X); efferent limb of the gag reflex

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Involvement in lateral medullary syndrome causes hoarseness, dysphagia, absent gag reflex and deviation of the uvula away from the lesion.

cards.name: Nuclei of solitary tract
cards.function: Visceral sensory nucleus receiving taste (CN VII, IX, X) and general visceral afferents from the carotid sinus and body, pharynx and thoracoabdominal viscera (CN IX, X).

details.label: Location
details.value: Dorsal medulla oblongata, lateral to the dorsal nucleus of the vagus nerve, surrounding the solitary tract

details.label: Function
details.value: Rostral (gustatory) part: taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue (chorda tympani), posterior third (CN IX) and epiglottis (CN X). Caudal part: baroreceptor, chemoreceptor and visceral reflexes; afferent limb of the gag and cough reflexes

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Ipsilateral loss of taste is part of the lateral medullary syndrome; the nucleus is the first relay of the baroreceptor reflex tested by carotid sinus massage.

cards.name: Posterior (dorsal) nucleus of vagus nerve
cards.function: Preganglionic parasympathetic nucleus of CN X for the thoracic and abdominal viscera as far as the left colic flexure.

details.label: Location
details.value: Dorsal medulla oblongata beneath the vagal trigone in the floor of the 4th ventricle, lateral to the nucleus of the hypoglossal nerve

details.label: Relations
details.value: Nuclei of the solitary tract lateral to it; area postrema near its caudal end

details.label: Function
details.value: Secretomotor to glands and motor to smooth muscle of the gut and airways; slows the heart together with the nucleus ambiguus

cards.name: Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve
cards.function: Somatic motor nucleus of CN XII supplying all intrinsic and extrinsic tongue muscles except palatoglossus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Paramedian dorsal medulla oblongata beneath the hypoglossal trigone in the floor of the 4th ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Its fibers pass forward to emerge between the pyramid and the olive; medial longitudinal fasciculus and medial lemniscus lie ventral to it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior spinal artery and paramedian branches of the vertebral artery

cards.pearl: Nuclear or nerve lesion: the protruded tongue deviates toward the side of the lesion, with atrophy and fasciculations; a supranuclear lesion deviates it away, without atrophy.

cards.name: Accessory nucleus
cards.function: Motor nucleus of the spinal root of CN XI supplying sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral part of the anterior horn of spinal cord segments C1-C5, continuing the line of the nucleus ambiguus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Rootlets emerge from the lateral surface of the cord between the anterior and posterior roots and ascend through the foramen magnum behind the denticulate ligament

cards.name: Medial longitudinal fasciculus
cards.function: Paramedian brain stem tract linking the vestibular nuclei with the nuclei of CN III, IV and VI and the upper cervical cord, coordinating conjugate eye movements with head position.

details.label: Location
details.value: Next to the midline just beneath the floor of the 4th ventricle and cerebral aqueduct, from the midbrain to the cervical spinal cord

details.label: Function
details.value: Carries fibers from the abducens nucleus to the opposite medial rectus subnucleus of the oculomotor nucleus for horizontal gaze

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Paramedian branches of the basilar artery

cards.pearl: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia: the eye on the side of the lesion fails to adduct on lateral gaze and the abducting eye shows nystagmus, with convergence preserved; bilateral in multiple sclerosis, unilateral in stroke.

cards.name: Cuneate fasciculus and cuneate tubercle
cards.function: Lateral part of the posterior column carrying fine touch, vibration and proprioception from the upper limb and upper trunk (above T6) to the cuneate nucleus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior funiculus of the cervical and upper thoracic cord and lower medulla oblongata, lateral to the gracile fasciculus; ends in the cuneate tubercle beside the lower rhomboid fossa

details.label: Relations
details.value: Gracile fasciculus and tubercle medial; inferior cerebellar peduncle lateral and above; second-order fibers cross and ascend as the medial lemniscus to the ventral posterolateral thalamic nucleus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior spinal arteries

cards.pearl: Posterior column disease (vitamin B12 deficiency, tabes dorsalis) causes ipsilateral loss of vibration and position sense with a positive Romberg sign.

cards.name: Gracile fasciculus and gracile tubercle
cards.function: Medial part of the posterior column carrying fine touch, vibration and proprioception from the lower limb and lower trunk (below T6) to the gracile nucleus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior funiculus beside the posterior median sulcus throughout the cord and lower medulla oblongata; ends in the gracile tubercle beside the obex

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cuneate fasciculus lateral; second-order fibers cross and ascend as the medial lemniscus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior spinal arteries

cards.pearl: Being most medial and longest, gracile fibers are affected first in vitamin B12 deficiency and tabes dorsalis, so vibration loss begins in the feet.

cards.name: Superior and inferior medullary vela
cards.function: Thin sheets of white matter that form the roof of the 4th ventricle above and below the cerebellum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior medullary velum stretches between the two superior cerebellar peduncles; inferior medullary velum extends from the nodule and flocculus toward the tela choroidea of the 4th ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lingula of the cerebellum lies on the superior velum and the trochlear nerves decussate in it; the median aperture lies in the roof below the inferior velum

cards.name: Cerebellum
cards.function: Hindbrain structure that coordinates the timing, force and accuracy of movement, maintains balance and muscle tone, and supports motor learning; each hemisphere controls the ipsilateral side of the body.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior cranial fossa beneath the tentorium cerebelli, behind the pons, medulla oblongata and 4th ventricle

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Vermis and two hemispheres. Anterior lobe, posterior lobe and flocculonodular lobe, separated by the primary fissure and posterolateral (dorsolateral) fissure; horizontal fissure divides the posterior lobe

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery, anterior inferior cerebellar artery and posterior inferior cerebellar artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Joined to the brain stem by the superior, middle and inferior cerebellar peduncles; transverse and sigmoid sinuses and occipital bone behind; falx cerebelli in the posterior cerebellar notch

cards.pearl: Hemisphere lesion: ipsilateral limb ataxia, dysmetria, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia. Midline (vermis) lesion: truncal and gait ataxia. Cerebellar hemorrhage or infarct with swelling is a neurosurgical emergency because it compresses the 4th ventricle and brain stem.

cards.name: Vermis of cerebellum
cards.function: Midline part of the cerebellum that controls axial and proximal muscles for posture, gait and eye movements.

details.label: Location
details.value: Median strip between the two hemispheres, from the superior medullary velum around to the inferior medullary velum

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior vermis: lingula (I), central lobule (II and III), culmen (IV and V), declive (VI), folium (VIIA). Inferior vermis: tuber (VIIB), pyramid (VIII), uvula (IX), nodule (X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery (superior vermis) and posterior inferior cerebellar artery (inferior vermis)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Roof of the 4th ventricle in front; straight sinus and tentorium cerebelli above; projects to the fastigial nuclei

cards.pearl: Alcohol-related degeneration of the anterior superior vermis gives a wide-based gait with relatively normal arm coordination; medulloblastoma arises in the vermis in children.

cards.name: Anterior lobe of cerebellum
cards.function: Part of the cerebellum in front of the primary fissure (spinocerebellum); receives spinocerebellar input and regulates muscle tone and gait.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior surface in front of the primary fissure

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Vermis: lingula (I), central lobule (II and III), culmen (IV and V). Hemisphere: wing of central lobule and quadrangular lobule (H IV and V)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Selectively degenerates in chronic alcohol use and thiamine deficiency: broad-based staggering gait with heel-to-shin ataxia.

cards.name: Posterior lobe of cerebellum
cards.function: Largest lobe, between the primary and posterolateral fissures (mostly cerebrocerebellum); receives cortical input through the pontine nuclei and plans and coordinates skilled limb movement.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the primary fissure on the superior surface and most of the inferior surface

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Vermis: declive (VI), folium (VIIA), tuber (VIIB), pyramid (VIII), uvula (IX). Hemisphere: simple lobule (H VI), superior semilunar (anseriform) lobule (H VIIA), inferior semilunar (caudal) lobule (H VIIB), biventer lobule (H VIII), tonsil

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery above, posterior inferior and anterior inferior cerebellar arteries below

details.label: Relations
details.value: Horizontal fissure separates the superior and inferior semilunar lobules; outputs through the dentate nucleus and superior cerebellar peduncle

cards.pearl: Lateral hemisphere lesions give ipsilateral dysmetria, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia and scanning speech.

cards.name: Flocculonodular lobe
cards.function: Oldest part of the cerebellum (vestibulocerebellum); connected with the vestibular nuclei to control balance and eye movements.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface in front of the posterolateral (dorsolateral) fissure, beside the 4th ventricle

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Nodule (X) of the vermis and the flocculus (H X) of each hemisphere, joined by the peduncle of the flocculus

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery (nodule) and anterior inferior cerebellar artery (flocculus)

cards.pearl: Midline tumors here (medulloblastoma, ependymoma) cause truncal ataxia with falls and nystagmus before limb signs appear.

cards.name: Lingula (I)
cards.function: Smallest and most anterior lobule of the superior vermis.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lies on the superior medullary velum between the superior cerebellar peduncles

details.label: Relations
details.value: Central lobule above and behind; 4th ventricle in front; trochlear nerve decussation in the velum beneath

cards.name: Central lobule (II and III)
cards.function: Lobule of the superior vermis in the anterior lobe; extends laterally on each side as the wing of the central lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: In the anterior cerebellar notch between the lingula in front and the culmen behind

details.label: Parts
details.value: Central lobule (vermis) and wing of central lobule (hemisphere)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior colliculi and superior cerebellar peduncles in front

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Culmen (IV and V)
cards.function: Highest lobule of the superior vermis, the largest vermal part of the anterior lobe; continuous laterally with the quadrangular lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior vermis between the central lobule and the primary fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Declive behind, across the primary fissure; straight sinus and tentorium cerebelli above; great cerebral vein (of Galen) in front

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: The culmen and adjacent anterior vermis bear the brunt of alcoholic cerebellar degeneration.

cards.name: Declive (VI)
cards.function: Sloping lobule of the superior vermis just behind the primary fissure; continuous laterally with the simple lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior vermis between the primary fissure in front and the folium behind

details.label: Relations
details.value: Culmen in front; simple lobule (H VI) on each side

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Folium (VIIA)
cards.function: Thin lobule at the posterior end of the superior vermis; continuous laterally with the superior semilunar lobules.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior cerebellar notch, between the declive above and the tuber below, at the horizontal fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior semilunar (anseriform) lobule on each side; falx cerebelli behind

cards.name: Tuber (VIIB)
cards.function: First lobule of the inferior vermis; continuous laterally with the inferior semilunar lobules. With the declive and folium it forms the oculomotor vermis that calibrates saccades.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior vermis just below the horizontal fissure, behind the pyramid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Folium above; pyramid in front; inferior semilunar (caudal) lobule on each side

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Pyramid (VIII)
cards.function: Lobule of the inferior vermis; continuous laterally with the biventer lobules.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior vermis between the tuber behind and the uvula in front, separated from the uvula by the secondary (postpyramidal) fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Biventer lobule (H VIII) on each side

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Uvula (IX)
cards.function: Lobule of the inferior vermis lying between the two tonsils; involved with the nodule in vestibular control.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior vermis between the secondary (postpyramidal) fissure and the posterolateral (dorsolateral) fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tonsil on each side; nodule in front; roof of the 4th ventricle and median aperture nearby

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Nodule (X)
cards.function: Most anterior lobule of the inferior vermis and midline part of the flocculonodular lobe; regulates balance and the vestibulo-ocular reflex.

details.label: Location
details.value: Projects into the roof of the 4th ventricle, in front of the uvula across the posterolateral (dorsolateral) fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior medullary velum attaches to it and connects it with the flocculus; choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle beside it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Nodule lesions cause truncal ataxia, positional vertigo and periodic alternating nystagmus.

cards.name: Quadrangular lobule (H IV and V)
cards.function: Hemispheric part of the anterior lobe, lateral to the culmen; receives spinocerebellar input from the limbs.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere in front of the primary fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Wing of central lobule in front; simple lobule behind; tentorium cerebelli above

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Simple lobule (H VI)
cards.function: Hemispheric lobule just behind the primary fissure, lateral to the declive; also termed the posterior quadrangular lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior surface of the cerebellar hemisphere between the primary fissure and the postlunate fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Quadrangular lobule in front; superior semilunar (anseriform) lobule behind

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Superior semilunar (anseriform) lobule (H VIIA)
cards.function: Large hemispheric lobule of the posterior lobe above the horizontal fissure; part of the cerebrocerebellum for planning skilled movement and cognitive functions.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior part of the superior surface of the hemisphere, between the postlunate fissure and the horizontal fissure

details.label: Relations
details.value: Continuous medially with the folium; inferior semilunar lobule below; transverse sinus behind

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Inferior semilunar (caudal) lobule (H VIIB)
cards.function: Hemispheric lobule of the posterior lobe below the horizontal fissure; its anterior strip is also termed the gracile lobule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior part of the inferior surface of the hemisphere, between the horizontal fissure and the biventer lobule

details.label: Relations
details.value: Continuous medially with the tuber; superior semilunar lobule above; biventer lobule in front

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery and anterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Biventer lobule (H VIII)
cards.function: Two-part hemispheric lobule on the inferior surface, lateral to the tonsil and continuous medially with the pyramid.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the hemisphere between the inferior semilunar lobule behind and the tonsil and flocculus in front

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tonsil medially across the retrotonsillar fissure; rests on the floor of the posterior cranial fossa

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.name: Tonsil of cerebellum
cards.function: Rounded hemispheric lobule on the inferior surface beside the uvula, lying just above the foramen magnum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferomedial part of each hemisphere, lateral to the uvula and behind the medulla oblongata

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medulla oblongata and 4th ventricle in front; posterior inferior cerebellar artery loops around it; posterior cerebellomedullary cistern below; biventer lobule laterally

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum (posterior fossa mass, or lumbar puncture with raised pressure) compresses the medulla: apnea and death. Chiari I malformation is chronic descent of the tonsils with headache and syringomyelia.

cards.name: Flocculus (H X)
cards.function: Small hemispheric lobule of the flocculonodular lobe that adjusts the vestibulo-ocular reflex and smooth pursuit.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior inferior surface of the hemisphere at the cerebellopontine angle, below the middle cerebellar peduncle

details.label: Parts
details.value: Joined to the nodule by the peduncle of the flocculus along the inferior medullary velum

details.label: Relations
details.value: Facial (CN VII) and vestibulocochlear (CN VIII) nerves lie just in front; choroid plexus of the 4th ventricle emerges from the lateral aperture beside it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: A vestibular schwannoma in the cerebellopontine angle compresses the flocculus and CN VIII: hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance and gaze-evoked nystagmus.

cards.name: Cerebellar nuclei
cards.function: Four paired deep nuclei that receive the inhibitory output of Purkinje cells and give rise to nearly all efferent fibers of the cerebellum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Embedded in the white matter of the cerebellum in the roof of the 4th ventricle

details.label: Divisions
details.value: From lateral to medial: dentate, emboliform, globose and fastigial nuclei

details.label: Function
details.value: Dentate, emboliform and globose nuclei project through the superior cerebellar peduncle to the red nucleus and ventral lateral thalamic nucleus; fastigial nucleus projects to the vestibular nuclei and reticular formation

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: The dentate nucleus is the usual site of hypertensive cerebellar hemorrhage.

cards.name: Superior cerebellar peduncle
cards.function: Main outflow of the cerebellum, carrying fibers from the dentate, emboliform and globose nuclei to the opposite red nucleus and thalamus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Runs from the cerebellum up to the midbrain, forming the lateral wall of the upper 4th ventricle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior medullary velum spans between the two peduncles; fibers cross in the decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncles at the level of the inferior colliculus; also carries the afferent anterior spinocerebellar tract

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Because cerebellar output crosses here and the corticospinal tract crosses back at the pyramids, cerebellar signs are ipsilateral to the lesion; a peduncle lesion gives marked ipsilateral intention tremor.

cards.name: Middle cerebellar peduncle
cards.function: Largest cerebellar peduncle; carries pontocerebellar fibers from the opposite pontine nuclei, relaying cerebral cortical input to the cerebellar hemisphere.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral continuation of the basilar part of the pons into the cerebellar hemisphere

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trigeminal nerve (CN V) emerges at its junction with the pons; flocculus and the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves lie below it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery and pontine arteries

cards.pearl: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery infarction (lateral pontine syndrome) involves this peduncle: ipsilateral ataxia with facial palsy, deafness and vertigo.

cards.name: Inferior cerebellar peduncle
cards.function: Connects the medulla and spinal cord with the cerebellum; carries the posterior spinocerebellar, cuneocerebellar, olivocerebellar and vestibulocerebellar fibers.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterolateral medulla oblongata, ascending lateral to the lower 4th ventricle and turning back into the cerebellum medial to the middle peduncle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cuneate tubercle below; cochlear nuclei on its surface; lateral recess of the 4th ventricle curves around it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery

cards.pearl: Its involvement accounts for the ipsilateral limb ataxia of lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome.

cards.name: Eyeball
cards.function: Globe of the eye: three concentric coats enclosing the refractive media that focus light on the retina.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior part of the orbit, enclosed in the bulbar sheath (Tenon's capsule) and moved by the extrinsic eye muscles

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Fibrous layer: cornea and sclera. Vascular layer: choroid, ciliary body and iris. Inner layer: retina (optic part, ciliary part and iridial part). Contents: aqueous humor in the anterior and posterior chambers, lens, vitreous body

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Ophthalmic artery: central retinal artery, short and long posterior ciliary arteries, anterior ciliary arteries; drained by the vorticose veins and central retinal vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic nerve (CN II) leaves posteriorly, medial to the posterior pole; bulbar conjunctiva covers the anterior sclera

cards.pearl: Axial length sets refraction: a long globe is myopic, a short globe hyperopic. A penetrating injury of one globe risks sympathetic ophthalmia in the other.

cards.name: Cornea
cards.function: Transparent avascular front of the fibrous layer; the main refracting surface of the eye.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior one-sixth of the eyeball, joined to the sclera at the corneoscleral junction (limbus)

details.label: Parts
details.value: Corneal epithelium, stroma, posterior limiting lamina (Descemet's membrane) and posterior epithelium (endothelium)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior chamber behind; bulbar conjunctiva ends at its margin; sensory supply from the long ciliary nerves (nasociliary nerve, CN V1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Avascular; nourished by aqueous humor, tears and limbal capillaries

cards.pearl: Corneal reflex: afferent CN V1, efferent CN VII. Herpes simplex keratitis shows dendritic ulcers on fluorescein; contact lens wearers are at risk of Pseudomonas keratitis. Kayser-Fleischer rings are copper in Descemet's membrane.

cards.name: Sclera
cards.function: Opaque white fibrous coat forming the posterior five-sixths of the eyeball; maintains its shape and gives insertion to the extrinsic eye muscles.

details.label: Location
details.value: From the cornea to the optic nerve, where it is continuous with the meningeal sheath of the optic nerve

details.label: Parts
details.value: Scleral spur and scleral venous sinus (canal of Schlemm) at the corneoscleral junction; lamina cribrosa of sclera where optic nerve fibers leave

details.label: Relations
details.value: Episcleral space and bulbar sheath outside; perichoroidal space and choroid inside; pierced by the ciliary arteries and nerves and the vorticose veins

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Episcleral arteries from the anterior ciliary arteries; posterior ciliary arteries

cards.pearl: Blue sclerae suggest osteogenesis imperfecta; scleritis (deep boring pain, associated with rheumatoid arthritis) must be distinguished from benign episcleritis. Jaundice shows first in the overlying conjunctiva.

cards.name: Choroid
cards.function: Pigmented vascular layer between the sclera and retina that nourishes the outer retina (rods and cones) and absorbs stray light.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior part of the vascular layer, from the optic nerve to the ora serrata, where it continues as the ciliary body

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Short posterior ciliary arteries; drained by the vorticose veins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Perichoroidal space and sclera outside; pigment epithelium of the retina firmly attached inside

cards.pearl: When the central retinal artery is occluded the fovea, supplied by the choroid, stays red against pale retina - the cherry-red spot. The choroid is the commonest site of intraocular melanoma and of metastasis.

cards.name: Ciliary body
cards.function: Ring of the vascular layer between choroid and iris; its processes secrete aqueous humor and its muscle changes the shape of the lens for accommodation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the corneoscleral junction, from the ora serrata to the root of the iris

details.label: Parts
details.value: Ciliary processes, orbiculus ciliaris and ciliary muscle (meridional and circular fibers); covered by the ciliary part of the retina

details.label: Function
details.value: Ciliary muscle contraction (parasympathetic, CN III via the ciliary ganglion) relaxes the zonular fibers so the lens rounds up for near vision

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Long posterior ciliary and anterior ciliary arteries forming the major arterial circle of the iris

cards.pearl: Aqueous production is reduced by beta-blockers (timolol), alpha-2 agonists and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (acetazolamide) in the treatment of glaucoma.

cards.name: Iris
cards.function: Pigmented contractile diaphragm in front of the lens whose central opening, the pupil, regulates the amount of light entering the eye.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the cornea and the lens, attached peripherally to the ciliary body; separates the anterior chamber from the posterior chamber

details.label: Parts
details.value: Sphincter pupillae muscle, dilator pupillae muscle, folds of iris, pigment epithelium (iridial part of retina)

details.label: Function
details.value: Sphincter pupillae: parasympathetic (CN III, ciliary ganglion, short ciliary nerves) - miosis. Dilator pupillae: sympathetic (superior cervical ganglion, long ciliary nerves) - mydriasis

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Major and minor arterial circles of the iris

cards.pearl: Horner syndrome: miosis, ptosis, anhidrosis. Anterior uveitis (iritis): painful red eye with photophobia and a small irregular pupil, associated with HLA-B27 disease. Lisch nodules of the iris occur in neurofibromatosis type 1.

cards.name: Lens
cards.function: Transparent biconvex body that fine-tunes focus; it becomes more convex for near vision when the ciliary muscle contracts.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the iris and pupil, in front of the vitreous body, suspended from the ciliary processes by the zonular fibers (suspensory ligament of lens)

details.label: Parts
details.value: Capsule of lens, cortex, nucleus of lens; equator and axis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Posterior chamber and iris in front; vitreous body behind

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Avascular; nourished by aqueous humor

cards.pearl: Cataract (opacity: age, diabetes, corticosteroids) causes painless gradual visual loss with glare. Presbyopia is loss of lens elasticity with age. Lens dislocation: upward in Marfan syndrome, downward in homocystinuria.

cards.name: Zonular fibers (suspensory ligament of lens)
cards.function: Fine fibers that suspend the lens from the ciliary body and transmit ciliary muscle tension to the lens capsule.

details.label: Location
details.value: Run from the ciliary processes and orbiculus ciliaris to the capsule of the lens around its equator, crossing the posterior chamber

details.label: Function
details.value: Taut when the ciliary muscle is relaxed (flat lens, distance vision); slack when it contracts (round lens, near vision)

cards.pearl: Made of fibrillin: defective in Marfan syndrome, causing ectopia lentis.

cards.name: Anterior chamber
cards.function: Aqueous-filled space between the cornea and the iris; aqueous humor drains from its angle into the scleral venous sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Behind the cornea, in front of the iris and pupil

details.label: Relations
details.value: Communicates with the posterior chamber through the pupil; iridocorneal angle at its periphery

cards.pearl: Blood in the anterior chamber is a hyphema (trauma); pus is a hypopyon (infectious keratitis, endophthalmitis). Cells and flare on slit lamp indicate anterior uveitis.

cards.name: Posterior chamber
cards.function: Narrow aqueous-filled space behind the iris into which the ciliary processes secrete aqueous humor.

details.label: Location
details.value: Between the iris in front and the lens, zonular fibers and ciliary processes behind

details.label: Function
details.value: Aqueous humor flows from here through the pupil to the anterior chamber

cards.pearl: If the iris sticks to the lens (pupillary block), aqueous trapped in the posterior chamber bows the iris forward and closes the angle.

cards.name: Iridocorneal angle and scleral venous sinus (canal of Schlemm)
cards.function: Drainage angle of the anterior chamber: aqueous humor filters through the trabecular meshwork into the scleral venous sinus and on to the anterior ciliary veins.

details.label: Location
details.value: Periphery of the anterior chamber where the cornea, sclera, ciliary body and root of the iris meet

details.label: Parts
details.value: Trabecular meshwork and spaces of the iridocorneal angle (of Fontana), pectinate ligament, scleral spur, scleral venous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Ciliary muscle (meridional fibers) attaches to the scleral spur, so its contraction opens the meshwork

cards.pearl: Acute angle-closure glaucoma: painful red eye, halos, fixed mid-dilated pupil, hard globe - precipitated by mydriatics; an emergency. Open-angle glaucoma: painless peripheral field loss with optic disc cupping from reduced trabecular outflow.

cards.name: Vitreous body
cards.function: Transparent gel that fills the vitreous chamber behind the lens, maintaining the shape of the eyeball and holding the retina against the choroid.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior four-fifths of the eyeball, between the lens and the retina

details.label: Parts
details.value: Traversed by the hyaloid canal, the remnant of the fetal hyaloid artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Attached most firmly at the ora serrata and around the optic disc

cards.pearl: Posterior vitreous detachment causes flashes and floaters and can tear the retina. Vitreous hemorrhage (proliferative diabetic retinopathy) causes sudden painless visual loss with loss of the red reflex.

cards.name: Retina
cards.function: Inner light-sensitive layer of the eyeball; photoreceptors signal through bipolar cells to ganglion cells, whose axons form the optic nerve.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lines the inside of the eyeball from the optic disc to the pupillary margin

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Optic (visual) part of retina, ending at the ora serrata; ciliary part of retina; iridial part of retina. Landmarks: macula with fovea centralis, optic disc

details.label: Parts
details.value: Pigment cells, rods and cones, horizontal cells, bipolar cells, amacrine cells, ganglion cells

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Inner layers: central retinal artery (superior and inferior temporal and nasal retinal arterioles). Outer layers including photoreceptors: choroid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Vitreous body inside; choroid outside

cards.pearl: Retinal detachment (curtain coming down, flashes, floaters) separates the neural retina from the pigment epithelium. Central retinal artery occlusion: sudden painless monocular blindness with a cherry-red spot.

cards.name: Macula and fovea centralis
cards.function: Central area of the retina specialized for high-acuity and color vision; the fovea contains only cones.

details.label: Location
details.value: At the posterior pole of the eyeball, lateral (temporal) to the optic disc

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior macular arterioles (central retinal artery) around it; the avascular fovea is nourished by the choroid

details.label: Function
details.value: Has a disproportionately large representation in the lateral geniculate body and at the occipital pole

cards.pearl: Age-related macular degeneration causes loss of central vision with metamorphopsia: dry (drusen) or wet (choroidal neovascularization, treated with anti-VEGF). Diabetic macular edema is the leading cause of visual loss in diabetes.

cards.name: Optic disc
cards.function: Point where ganglion cell axons converge to leave the eye as the optic nerve and where the central retinal vessels enter and leave; it has no photoreceptors (the blind spot).

details.label: Location
details.value: Medial (nasal) to the macula and posterior pole

details.label: Relations
details.value: Central retinal artery and vein emerge at its center; fibers pass through the lamina cribrosa of sclera; meningeal sheath of the optic nerve with its subarachnoid space reaches the back of the disc

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Short posterior ciliary arteries and the central retinal artery

cards.pearl: Papilledema (swollen disc with blurred margins) reflects raised intracranial pressure transmitted along the optic nerve sheath. Glaucoma enlarges the cup-to-disc ratio; a pale disc indicates optic atrophy.

cards.name: Bulbar sheath (Tenon's capsule)
cards.function: Thin fascial socket around the eyeball from the optic nerve to near the cornea, in which the globe rotates.

details.label: Location
details.value: Surrounds the sclera, separated from it by the episcleral space

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pierced by the tendons of the extrinsic eye muscles, on which it is reflected as muscular fascia; thickened below as the suspensory ligament of the eyeball; bulbar conjunctiva covers it anteriorly

cards.pearl: Sub-Tenon injection delivers local anesthetic for eye surgery; after enucleation the sheath forms the socket for the implant.

cards.name: Spinal cord
cards.function: Part of the central nervous system in the vertebral canal that carries ascending and descending tracts and mediates segmental reflexes; gives rise to 31 pairs of spinal nerves.

details.label: Location
details.value: From the medulla oblongata at the foramen magnum to the conus medullaris at about the L1-L2 vertebral level in adults

details.label: Parts
details.value: Cervical enlargement (brachial plexus) and lumbar enlargement (lumbar and sacral plexuses); conus medullaris; filum terminale internum and externum; cauda equina

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior spinal artery (anterior two-thirds) and paired posterior spinal arteries, reinforced by segmental medullary arteries

details.label: Relations
details.value: C1 spinal nerve exits above the C1 vertebra and C8 below C7, so there are 8 cervical nerves but 7 cervical vertebrae; spinal dura mater ends at S2

cards.pearl: Lumbar puncture is done at L3-L4 or L4-L5, below the conus medullaris. Cauda equina syndrome: saddle anesthesia, urinary retention and bilateral leg weakness - a surgical emergency.

cards.name: Gray matter and white matter of spinal cord
cards.function: In cross section the cord has a central H-shaped gray matter of neuronal cell bodies surrounded by white matter funiculi of ascending and descending tracts.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Gray matter: anterior horn (lower motor neurons), posterior horn (sensory relay) and lateral horn (preganglionic sympathetic neurons, T1-L2). White matter: anterior, lateral and posterior funiculi

details.label: Function
details.value: Posterior funiculus: gracile and cuneate fasciculi (vibration, proprioception). Lateral funiculus: lateral corticospinal tract and spinothalamic tract. Central canal lies in the gray commissure

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior horns and anterior and lateral funiculi; posterior spinal arteries supply the posterior funiculi and horns

cards.pearl: Brown-Sequard hemisection: ipsilateral weakness and loss of vibration and proprioception, contralateral loss of pain and temperature. Anterior spinal artery syndrome spares the posterior columns. Syringomyelia gives a cape-like loss of pain and temperature.

cards.name: Spinal meninges and denticulate ligament
cards.function: Dura mater, arachnoid mater and pia mater continue from the cranial cavity around the spinal cord; lateral pial extensions anchor the cord within the dural sac.

details.label: Parts
details.value: Spinal dura mater (single layer, separated from the vertebrae by fat and the internal vertebral venous plexus in the epidural space), arachnoid mater, subarachnoid space, pia mater, denticulate ligament

details.label: Location
details.value: The dural sac extends from the foramen magnum to S2; the filum terminale externum continues to the coccyx

details.label: Relations
details.value: Denticulate ligament attaches to the dura between the anterior and posterior roots; each root pair carries a meningeal sheath to the intervertebral foramen; the spinal root of the accessory nerve ascends behind the ligament

cards.pearl: Epidural anesthesia is placed in the fat-filled epidural space outside the dura; spinal anesthesia and lumbar puncture enter the subarachnoid space. A spinal epidural abscess presents with fever, back pain and progressive neurologic deficit.
